1. “No Man Ever Could Have Done It; but God Did It”: Durham’s Conversion, Spirit Baptism and Call

William H. Durham, “Personal Testimony of Pastor Durham,” The Pentecostal Testimony, Vol. II, No. 3 (August 1912), pp. 2–5 (first printed March 1909; this version rewritten c. 1911); “Our Book and Other Personal Matters,” The Pentecostal Testimony, Vol. I, No. 8 (August 1911), p. 16; “In Memoriam” (unsigned), The Pentecostal Testimony, Vol. II, No. 3 (August 1912), pp. 2–3. Primary sources; page numbers from the OCR page marks, to be checked against the scans; the interpretations are the authors’.

CTS note: William H. Durham (1873–1912) was pastor of the North Avenue Mission in Chicago and editor of The Pentecostal Testimony. He was baptized in the Spirit at the Azusa Street Mission in Los Angeles on 2 March 1907, under its pastor William J. Seymour. The testimony given here is the version rewritten about 1911 and reprinted after his death; the 1909 wording differs in places. The “claim” theory is the teaching that one may receive the Spirit simply by claiming Him in faith, without any outward sign; to “tarry” is to wait in prayer; to “come through” is to complete the baptism by speaking in tongues. The book Durham promised was never published. “In Memoriam” is unsigned and was written by his Los Angeles assembly after his death on 7 July 1912; its date “February 1910” should read 1911. “[illegible]” marks words the OCR does not preserve.

Personal Testimony of Pastor Durham

(Rewritten and published to glorify Jesus.)

I was born and raised in the State of Kentucky where I united with the Baptist Church about the year 1891. I was sincere at the time, but I was not converted. Therefore my experience was a great disappointment to me, for I knew that, as a member of the church, I ought to have an experience; but I had no joy or peace, or knowledge of salvation. In the year 1898, in the State of Minnesota, the Holy Spirit deeply convicted me of sin. This came about through reading the Word of God; and being convinced of its truth, I was made to see that I was a guilty sinner. The Spirit was so faithful in dealing with me, that I could find no rest or peace, until I resolved to yield myself to God the best I knew how and call upon Him for mercy. The moment I did so, the Holy Spirit revealed Jesus Christ to me hanging on the Cross, and said to me, “Christ died for your sins.” Faith instantly sprung up in my heart to accept Him as my full Savior, and the moment I did so, I felt the quickening power of the Spirit, was made a new creature in Christ, and unutterable joy filled my soul. The Spirit bore faithful witness to me, that I was a child of God. I knew beyond doubt, that I was washed in the Blood of Jesus, and the peace that passes all understanding filled my soul.

I would have as soon met God as my dearest friend. I had no one to tell me that the next step was to be buried with Him, in Whom I had died and had been made alive. Had I been taught the truth, as the Apostles taught it, had I been baptized and had hands laid on me, I would have at once received the Holy Ghost; I should then have been taught to reckon that I was “dead indeed,” and that I was to live and walk only in the Holy Spirit; but I could not walk in Him Whom I had not yet received. Like thousands of others, I drifted. After two years of investigating the theories of men and struggling in every way known to me to obtain the experience of sanctification, and failing in all, I finally had grace given me from God to yield myself to Him, and trust the merits of the Blood alone, just as I had done three years before, when as a trembling sinner, I stood before the Cross and had a glimpse of the glorious Son of God, who died thereon, given me.

To my unutterable joy this step brought me back into the same state of entire sanctification and heavenly rest, peace and joy, which I had the first time I stood in the same place. As in the case of all who remain under the Blood, the Spirit dealt wondrously with me. The influence of His presence with me was so real and precious, that I really thought I had received the gift of the Holy Ghost. My greatest difficulty was in harmonizing my experience with that in the Acts of the Apostles. My difficulty was, that I mistook soul rest and peace, and the sweet holy joy of salvation, and the witness and influence of the Spirit, for the gift of the Spirit. O, how many are making this sad mistake! I knew my experience did not measure up to the standard of the Acts of the Apostles, but like all holiness teachers and people, that I have met, I either kept out of the book of Acts, or confounded the wonderful outpourings of the Holy Spirit recorded there, with sanctification.

What a sad mistake. What could be more ridiculous than the teaching, that it was sanctification, or any other work of grace, the Apostles received on the day of Pentecost?

In the spring of 1906, I heard of the mighty outpouring of the Holy Spirit in the City of Los Angeles, accompanied by the speaking in other tongues. It brought joy to my heart, and I told my people that I had no doubt, that it was a mighty work of God. I believed in all the gifts of the Holy Spirit, including tongues, and had longed to see them in operation in the church. But when I heard the teaching, that speaking in tongues was the evidence of the baptism in the Holy Ghost, it stirred me to the depths. I fearlessly denounced this point of doctrine as false; but when I saw the people who were filled with the Spirit and speaking in tongues, I knew that their experience was genuine. I simply thought they were wrong on this point. If this teaching were true, I had not the baptism. This would mean, that I would have to come down and take the place of a seeker. It is easy to see how hard it would be for me to do this, as I had preached the Gospel for about five years and all the time professed to have the Holy Ghost, and tried to lead others into the same experience. So I said, “no man can ever convince me, that I have not received the Holy Ghost.” No man ever could have done it; but God did it.

In the fall of 1906, the Spirit began to fall on people here in Chicago. Among the first to be baptized in the Spirit and speak in tongues were a number that I had labored with for three years and had never doubted that they had the same experience I had; I saw that they were filled with a joy, power and glory they never had before; that they had a love for God and souls, they never had before; and when I saw them stand up, with their faces shining with the [illegible] of Heaven, and heard them tell of the increased [illegible] and power, and then heard them speak and sing in tongues, it settled the question with me. I saw and heard for the first time in my life something that measured up to the teachings of the Book of Acts. I at once went down before God and became an earnest seeker; I found at once that the old “claim” theory was exploded by this movement. I could not kneel at the altar, and claim the Holy Ghost and go away. This was a real experience. I must wait until He came. Finding it necessary to drop my pastoral duties for a time, I did so, and went to Los Angeles to tarry before God until He met me.

I shall never forget my first day in Azusa Street Mission. As soon as I entered the place, I saw that God was there. There were hundreds of people present, yet no man seemed to have anything to do with what was happening. The Holy Ghost seemed to have perfect control. My soul was melted down before the Lord. After a few hymns had been sung, a wave of power and glory seemed to sweep over the place, and a song broke forth in the Spirit, known in this movement as the Heavenly Anthem. It was the sweetest music that ever fell on my ears. It was the Spirit of God Himself, and I knew it. I could not sing in that choir, though I would have given much to do so. I had not received Him, who was doing the singing. I saw clearly, for the first time, the difference between having the influence and presence of the Spirit with us, and having Him dwell within us in person.

Now began a time of waiting and real heart searching. I became more helpless from day to day. Everything seemed to slip away from me. The works that I had formerly rejoiced in, and the experiences that I had gloried in could not help me now. I reached the place that I could truly say with David, “My heart and my flesh crieth out for the living God.” I had done everything I knew to do, and refused to struggle more. I simply waited, claiming God’s promise, trusting in the merits of the Blood of Christ alone.

On the 26th day of February, 1907, I went to the afternoon service. I was at the end of everything; and the Lord knew it. There were 30 or more people present in the prayer room. Three of God’s dear children came to me, and as they stood over me, one of them said, “Just cease trying to do anything, and surrender all to God.” I did so; when, O, joy, a thrill of power went through me, followed by another. Instantly it appeared as if everyone of my pores were suddenly opened and a mighty current of power turned into me from every side; and so great was the infilling, that it seemed as if the physical life would be crowded out of my body. I literally gasped for breath, and fell in a heap on the floor. My strength was gone, but I was perfectly conscious of everything; so kept lifting my heart to God and earnestly entreating Him to finish the work. So intense was my longing to have the work finished, that I was reaching Heavenward with one hand all the time. God knows best how to do His work. I am glad He did not finish the work the first time the power came upon me. My experience has been much more valuable as He gave it to me. No tongue could ever tell, what passed between God and my soul these first two hours I was under His power. It was glorious and wonderful. It was heaven. Such love, such sweetness, such a revelation of the Blood as the only remedy for sin, such a revelation of Christ as the only Savior, and many things that it is impossible for me to tell. After two hours He withdrew, leaving me the great benefit I had received from His visit, but with a consciousness that He Who had so wonderously wrought, had departed from me. I was disappointed; but knew He would return and finish His work. I now understand why he paid me this wonderful visit and left me without finishing the work. I meet many people who have had some wonderful experience in their lives, which they called the baptism in the Holy Ghost; and this blessed experience enables me to locate them. God has visited them, and when they contend that it is the baptism, I remember how the glory filled my own soul, and how everything within me seemed to be turned into love and sweetness, and how I walked more than a mile, with my very spirit within me whispering, “Glory to Jesus,” at every step. I also remember, that He made me to know that this was simply my own spirit’s being brought into a state of rapture, and that the baptism was not yet completed.

The Lord permitted me to walk in this state for two days and nights. Then, as I knelt before Him, the Spirit again fell on me. Again I fell to the floor, and for two hours His mighty power was upon me. This time there were more manifestations, shakings, etc. Still I did not get the baptism. In spite of my earnest pleadings, He again left me, and I was conscious that the work was not finished. I had come to believe that speaking in tongues was the evidence of the baptism; and besides this my own heart told me, there was more. The next night, I knelt at the altar again, holding before God the words of Christ, that if they ask for bread He will not give them a stone, etc. Again the Spirit fell on me, and again I went down under His mighty power. For three hours He wrought wondrously with me. I have never witnessed anything just like it. My body was worked in sections, a section at a time. Even the skin on my face was jerked and shaken; and finally I felt my lower jaw begin to quiver in a strange way. This continued for some time, when finally my throat began to enlarge and I felt my vocal organs being, as it were, drawn into a different shape. O, how strange and wonderful it all was to me and how blessed it was to be thus in the hands of God. Last of all I felt my tongue begin to move and my lips begin to produce strange sounds; which did not originate in my mind.

In a few moments He was speaking clearly through me in other tongues, and then I heard Brother Seymour, the Pastor say, “He is through now,” etc. He said that he had retired to rest early in the evening, and that the Spirit had spoken to him and said, “Brother Durham will get the baptism tonight,” and that he had arisen and come down. Then he lifted up his hand and prophesied that where I should preach the Holy Spirit would fall on the people. The Lord then permitted me to rise to my feet, and He, for Whom my soul had longed, did not leave me this time, but remained, and for a long time I could not help speaking in tongues.

O, how glorious it seemed to have the blessed Holy Ghost abiding within me, so that I was as conscious of His presence as I was of my own life, and O, how real the precious Blood of Christ and all that pertains to His work of redemption on the Cross of Calvary was made to me.

I have emphasized the Spirit’s dealing with me before He remained in me, to make it plain that one can have wonderful experiences and yet not receive the personal Holy Ghost. In fact, up to the time I saw the Spirit’s work in the Pentecostal movement, I had never seen anything so wonderful, as the operation of the Spirit upon me, in the two experiences I have described, before He finished His work and took up His abode within me; yet in neither one of them did I receive the Holy Spirit.

It is now nearly four years since I received the Holy Ghost, as He took up His abode within me, March 2nd, 1907. And every day of this time I have been perfectly conscious of His indwelling presence. The baptism is only the entrance into the Spirit-filled life, as after receiving Him, He teaches us all things, bringing to our remembrance the words of Jesus, bears His fruits in our lives, imparts His gifts unto us, searches and reveals the deep things of God, and guides us into all truth.

Dear reader, the Spirit may not deal with you just as He did with me; but when He comes within you, to take up His abode, He will speak in tongues and magnify God. Acts 2:4; 10:44–47; 19:6.

Our Book and Other Personal Matters

As hard as we toiled, before leaving Chicago, to finish the material for the book we have promised to write, we have found it impossible to do so. When the revival, reported in another article in this paper, commenced here, we saw at once that all our time and strength would be necessary to carry it on successfully, and there would necessarily be another delay with the book. At one time we thought to return to each one the money paid in for it, but then we remembered that most of those who have handed in a dollar, knowing the book was only prospective, have told us to keep the money and use it in the work as we thought best, if for any reason the book was not published. Then we had a standing notice that anyone desiring a refund could have it on receipt of notice that they desired it.

We believe the book is as sure to be published as the Lord tarries and permits us to live but cannot give the date. We desire the prayers of all the saints in a very special way for us in every department of the work, as it has grown and spread, till it requires wisdom and strength that is beyond human to carry it on. Never have we had such doors of opportunity open before us. Never have we had such opposition and persecution. Never were we so determined to go all the way with Jesus. Christ is all and in all. We will preach Him as such if the number of self-seekers, opposers, traitors and hypocrites should multiply a hundred fold. We are now preparing, in the will of the Lord, to move on up the Coast, and pitch the battle for God.

In most every town the saints are waiting for us. In the will of God we expect to stop at San Jose, Oakland, San Francisco, Seattle, Spokane and Portland, and at such other places as the Lord shall lead. We expect a battle in most, or all of these places, but the God of battles is with us, and that means victory. Will the saints in all these places begin to wait on God for a mighty outpouring when we shall come to their town.

For two years the Lord has been moving upon me much of the time to make myself an offering to the whole Pentecostal movement, and not to confine my labors to any particular field. In the fullest possible sense, I now am endeavoring to do this. Pray that my whole life may be laid at His feet, and used to the very best advantage for His glory, and the good of His people.

In Memoriam

On the seventh day of July, nineteen hundred and twelve, at ten minutes after eight in the morning, our beloved brother Durham entered into rest. His end was peaceful, and he gladly obeyed the divine summons to enter the Master’s presence. The following facts concerning his life will be gratefully received by all who knew him:

Wm. H. Durham was born in the state of Kentucky, in the year eighteen hundred and seventy-three. He joined a baptist church at the age of eighteen, but was not converted, and not until he had lost confidence in religion and wandered into sin, was he arrested by the Holy Spirit and put under conviction. Day by day this conviction deepened, until finally he resolved to yield and call upon God for mercy. Instantly the Spirit revealed to him Jesus hanging on the cross and said, “Christ died for your sins.” He believed it with all his heart, and instantly the Spirit witnessed that he was born again. This was in Minnesota in the year eighteen hundred and ninety-eight. He was soon after called of the Lord into active service, and wherever he went crowds came to the altar and were saved and healed. This continued until the light came on the baptism of the Holy Spirit, which he finally accepted, and travelled from Chicago to Los Angeles that he might wait on God unmolested by his pastoral duties. He was baptized in the Spirit on March 2nd, 1907, and returned to Chicago. And then began that wonderful ministry which astonished the world. Ten missions preaching the full gospel sprang up under his ministry in Chicago.

Ministers from far and near came to his mission and accepted the truth and went away filled with the Spirit.

He published Pentecostal Testimony which went all over the earth, and carried conviction wherever it went. Scores were converted through reading its pages, and many hundreds were convicted to seek for the baptism.

About eighteen months ago God led him to fearlessly proclaim the great truth, the finished work of Calvary. It met with strong opposition, but God confirmed the truth in such a way that men were forced to listen. In February 1910 [that is, 1911], he came to Los Angeles, the great Pentecostal centre, to deliver his message, and amidst persecution and opposition of every kind, God baptized hundreds in the Spirit in a few months, and established an assembly of over six hundred people who stand for the truths of the finished work of Calvary, and the baptism in the Holy Spirit.

Last February he went to Chicago much weakened by continual labors to hold a two weeks’ convention, and God gave him the greatest revival of modern times. God thus signifying to the world his approval of his servant up to the last. This wonderful revival, described on another page of this paper, was the greatest of his life. The material for the last edition of Pentecostal Testimony was prepared during this vigorous evangelistic campaign. This terrific strain brought about a general break down, and though our brother rallied again, it was only for a short time. He was given strength to visit the mission, and deliver his last message, expressing his conviction that God was going to take him home. It came as a great shock to the saints, and threw them on their faces before God. Many all night prayer meetings were held and many devoted saints in different parts of the country prayed night and day for weeks, but God saw that his work was finished, and while the saints were praying, the Spirit said to many of them, “He has finished his course, he has kept the faith.”

His last request to God was that he might be given strength to travel home to Los Angeles and see his beloved friends before he died. God graciously granted this request, and accordingly he left for Los Angeles on Tuesday, arriving here on Friday, July 5th, and early Sunday morning his Spirit went home to God.

We were all assembled for morning worship when the news came. The whole assembly went on their knees before God, and great lamentation followed. We felt our hearts melted together in a common sorrow, but we sorrow not as others that have no hope. “Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.”

The funeral services were precious. The body was brought down to the mission hall on the corner of 7th and Los Angeles Streets, where fully one thousand people were present. The service commenced at two o’clock P. M. and lasted for an hour, after which all the people viewed the remains. A large company then followed to the Inglewood cemetery, where we laid his body in the grave, with a certain and sure hope of a glorious resurrection at the sound of the first trump. “For the Lord Himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God; and the dead in Christ shall rise first; then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air; and so shall we ever be with the Lord” (1 Thessalonians 4:16–17). Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection; on such the second death hath no power.

We are glad to have known him, and though we keenly feel our loss, he has gone to be with Jesus, which is far better.

“Thus heaven is gathering one by one, / To its capacious breast, / All that is pure and permanent, / And beautiful and best.”

2. “The Bible Brand”: Spirit Baptism, Tongues and Manifestations

William H. Durham, “Manifestations Number II,” The Pentecostal Testimony, Vol. I, No. 5 (July 1910), pp. 6–9; “Speaking in Tongues Is the Evidence of the Baptism in the Holy Spirit,” The Pentecostal Testimony, Vol. II, No. 2 (May 1912), pp. 9–12. Editorial articles by Durham as editor. Primary sources; page numbers from the OCR page marks; the interpretations are the author’s.

CTS note: Durham held the doctrine later called “initial evidence”: everyone baptized in the Spirit speaks in tongues at that moment (Acts 2:4; 10:44–47; 19:6). He distinguished this sign from the gift of tongues in 1 Corinthians 12–14. Christians weigh the question differently: many Pentecostal churches still teach initial evidence; many charismatics and some Pentecostals regard tongues as one possible sign among others; other Christians hold that such gifts are not expected today. CTS presents these views without deciding between them. “Six years ago on the Pacific Coast” refers to the Azusa Street revival of 1906. George Fox (1624–1691) founded the Quakers; Peter Cartwright and Charles Finney were nineteenth-century American revival preachers. “Under the power” means overcome by God’s power, often falling to the floor. CTS has omitted one short clause in “Manifestations” ([…]).

Manifestations Number II

In a previous number of Pentecostal Testimony we published an article on manifestations which did much to clear up the subject for many; but still many questions are being asked and we feel that another article on the same subject is necessary. One thing is sure: Whenever there is a revival of considerable power there are sure to be manifestations. After all different opinions are expressed the facts remain the same. When the mighty power of God rested upon George Fox and the early Quakers there were visible manifestations of the Spirit’s power. The devil was aroused and awful persecution followed. Mr. Fox was imprisoned, mobbed, and shamefully treated in many ways. To our mind it was not so much his simple, plain preaching and dress that drew the fire of the devil as the manifestations of the Holy Ghost which accompanied his ministry. People not only heard the Word, but saw the power of God. They were compelled to acknowledge that there were supernatural manifestations following the powerful preaching of this humble man.

When God sends a man He always manifests His power through him and the devil is always stirred. When God sent Moses to Pharaoh to deliver His message, signs and wonders accompanied that message when it was delivered. As long as Moses lived God wrought wonders through him. So it was with Joshua and all the prophets. So it was with Jesus Christ Himself and with His apostles, and so has it ever been since the days of the apostles.

When signs and wonders cease it is a sure evidence that the Church has drifted away from God, and that God has withdrawn His presence from it. And in every case where the people set their faces to seek God and continue to do so till He returns to them, His return is evidenced and accompanied by signs and wonders. As stated, it was so in the days of Fox. It was notably so in the days of Wesley, Cartwright, Finney and many other mighty men that God has raised up to declare His Gospel. Further the manifestations have always been somewhat similar. The Quakers were so called because they shook and quaked under the power of the Spirit of God. In the days of Wesley, Finney and others, the people not only shook and trembled but fell under the power, sometimes in numbers, and often lay for hours. These manifestations have always stirred the devil. Cold, formal preachers and churches have always been aroused to action, and have generally opposed and hindered all they possibly could. The preachers know they ought to have power, and not having it, they feel that the easiest thing for them to do is to declare that the manifestations following the ministry of others are not of God, but honest souls are always convinced by the manifestations that God is working.

The manifestations in the present great outpouring of the Holy Ghost have been and still are something wonderful. All the manifestations witnessed in the great revivals of the last two hundred years seem to have reappeared and others that have not been seen before since the days of the Apostles, so far as I know. God has visited His people and mighty signs and wonders are following. God is repeating many of His wonderful works which have been seen in other ages. In this day when the miraculous is being scoffed at even by preachers and church members, God is reviving the miraculous. Just when men are denying the power of God, He is sending His power among those who believe Him. This power will increase among true believers till Jesus comes. God is a God of power: His works are works of power. And the devil and unbelieving men hate to see the mighty power of God being manifested, because they know men will be convinced thereby that God is the same and the works and teachings of men and devils will be overthrown.

From the beginning of the present great outpouring the opposers have severely criticised the wonderful manifestations of the Spirit of God, and have proven their ignorance of what God is doing, by the weakness of their arguments and criticisms. For a person to declare that the manifestations in the Pentecostal movement are psychological or a result of nervousness is sufficient proof to establish his ignorance of the subject in the mind of everyone who has experienced the manifestations of the Spirit in his life. I must state actual facts just as they are. To tell a man who has time and time again felt the literal power of God stream into his soul and body, and so fill him that he would fall helplessly to the floor and remain under the control of the power for several minutes or even an hour or more, and who at such times feels his soul filled with unutterable glory and praise to God, or feels a real burden of prayer and soul travail for the lost, that, because his body is shaken more or less at the time, it is all nervousness is to make yourself ridiculous in his eyes. To say that it is excitement or that we work ourselves up to this state is false.

Recently in a meeting in North Avenue mission there were nearly two hundred people in attendance and without any visible cause for it they were presently nearly all mightily under the power of God. We had just risen from our knees when wave after wave of power and glory swept over our souls and bodies, filling our souls with glory and praise, and shaking many of our bodies, and speaking in tongues and singing in the Spirit was heard on every side. People in all parts of the building were equally affected. This continued for nearly half an hour before the regular order of service could be continued. No person could deny that there was a supernatural power operating among the people. No one who heard the volume of praise which ascended to God and heard the name and power of Jesus Christ and His precious Blood exalted could doubt that it was the power of God. O how Satan hates this real visible power of God which can be seen and felt and which so clearly demonstrates the fact that God is working among His people!

But some will say, “I have seen manifestations which I cannot believe to be from God.” So have I. There never was a genuine work in progress that Satan did not get some counterfeit into it. Every great revival attracts not only honest seekers and well-balanced people, but cranks and fanatics as well. I never saw the exception. Every revivalist of any note has had his troubles with them, and we have had our full share. There is a host of them and they all desire to air their theories or ride their hobbies; but they are no proof that God is not working, but rather prove that He is working. But as the purpose of this article is not to deal with cranks and fanatics, we will return to the subject of manifestations.

There are three distinct kinds of manifestations. The first is produced by the direct operation of the Spirit of God. It is this one, and only this that we wish to defend. The other extreme is any manifestation which is produced by the direct operation of demon power. No one with any knowledge of Scripture can deny that the devil has power and that he gets control of people whenever possible. Between these two is what I would call manifestations of the flesh. There is much that could not be said to be of God, and yet I would not dare to say it was of the devil. My opinion is that many people are entirely too liberal with the devil. That is, they are too quick to ascribe to him any manifestation or work which they do not understand. Such people, as soon as they see a physical manifestation, are ready to cry out that it is the devil; simply because they do not understand it. If asked for proof that it is Satan they simply say: “O, God would never work in that way,” as though they were authority on what God will or will not do.

As some who in a general way believe in the Pentecostal movement are afraid of physical manifestations, we will deal briefly with these three kinds of manifestations mentioned, in the hope that many will be made to see the truth. While it would be wrong to say that every physical manifestation is of God, it is entirely wrong to say that any great per cent of them are from the devil. Nor is it correct to say that that which is physical is of the flesh, as so many do say. God is putting His power not only upon our spirits, but upon our bodies as well. Paul says, “The body is the temple of the Holy Spirit.” The Spirit of God comes upon and into our bodies, and physical manifestations are the inevitable result. So that a physical manifestation which is produced by the direct operation of the Holy Spirit is just as real and acceptable as a shout or similar Spiritual manifestation. To my mind, by far the greater part of physical manifestations which I have seen, such as shaking, falling under the power, etc., were produced by the direct operation of the Spirit of God upon the physical beings of His children. I have seen several cases, however, where I believe it was the flesh working. In other cases when God really works, folks become self-conscious and desire to be seen, and thus it becomes evident that while God is working the flesh is working also. In many genuine experiences the flesh is allowed to get in in some little measure, and God is hindered and the person does not have as beautiful an experience as he would, had he kept self entirely out of it. I would have to say that in a few cases, perhaps a half dozen or more, I have seen what I was compelled to believe was the power of Satan working, but it has generally been in persons who have at some time dabbled with Spiritualism […].

Some one will say, “If there have been cases where the enemy got hold of people, is it really safe for us to seek the experience?” Our answer is, that it is perfectly safe for any honest person to seek to be filled with the Holy Spirit, as the Blood of Christ in which they trust makes it impossible for Satan to touch them. They are in no more danger than an honest sinner is in when he is seeking God for salvation. In other words, we have too much confidence in God to believe He would allow an honest soul while seeking His face, and desiring to be filled with the Holy Spirit, to be taken possession of by the devil. If this could be, no one would be safe in seeking God for anything. The words of Christ on this line have great weight with us. He says, “If a son shall ask bread of anyone of you who is a father, will he give him a stone?” etc. There is no safer place under Heaven for an honest soul than seeking God for anything which He has promised to His children.

I would answer the oft repeated question of how to come to God for the baptism in the Holy Spirit in this way: come with a humble heart and mind, trusting the Blood of Christ alone, and ask Him for the gift of the Holy Spirit—not that you may be great and powerful, but that you may be brought into a right relationship to God, and possess your promised inheritance, and that Jesus Christ may be glorified through the Holy Spirit’s dwelling in you. To my mind, it is a sad mistake to seek God for His Spirit’s power with a desire prominent in your mind to do or be something. A person seeking power with a desire to do some great thing, who is not perfectly honest in his desire to be right with God, or who does not first seek to be fully cleansed in the Blood of Christ and made clean and pure in the sight of God, will not only fail to get anything from God, but is in grave danger of being taken possession of by some evil spirit, or receiving an awful rebuke from God, as Simon the sorcerer at the City of Samaria.

I wish to reaffirm that I believe there have been very few cases of demon possession, or manifestations produced by an evil spirit that have come under my observation. I cannot and do not believe it is possible for Satan to get possession of an honest person. It is my belief that every case of real demon power that has been witnessed in the Pentecostal or any other work has been that of some dishonest or unclean person. For a person, as many have done, to attribute all the physical manifestations to Satan, to my mind, is little short of blaspheming the Holy Spirit, as the manifestations of the power of God are so many and so wonderful, as well as so valuable, that it is an awful mistake to credit them to Satan.

There is really little resemblance between the manifestations of the Spirit of God and the manifestations of Satan. I can detect the workings of the devil as soon as I see them. He always leads people to do foolish and unscriptural things, that in the end do not profit; while the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal. Satan destroys body, mind and soul, fills with doubt, fear, envy and strife, destroys confidence in God and man, and in the Word of God. The power of God strengthens us bodily, mentally and spiritually, increases our faith in God and man, fills with love, joy and peace, deepens our love and strengthens faith in Jesus Christ the only Son of God, and in the blessed Word of God. Time and again have I had the power of God come upon me and prostrate me for several minutes, or even an hour. When the power would lift I would find myself wonderfully strengthened and rested in body and mind, and most wonderfully uplifted spiritually. In fact, my soul is filled with faith, love, joy, peace, confidence in God, and all other things that I understand to be from God as at no other time. Dare anyone say that I would receive such results if it were Satanic power that came upon me as some seem to think it is? It is disgusting to me to hear folks talk as though God allowed the devil to put his infernal power on His children, and make playthings of them a good part of the time. God’s children are under the Blood of Jesus Christ, and Satan has no power to touch them as long as they stay there; but let them watch and pray, and trust the blood continually, to keep them clean, lest the enemy get an advantage over them.

I believe we will see greater manifestations of the power of God as the dispensation draws to a close. God’s people are going down before Him in real humility and faith. And the nearer they get to Him the greater the degree of power which He puts upon them, and the greater the degree of power which produces the physical manifestations, which we are defending, the greater the results. This is why the devil hates and opposes the manifestations so. He knows they evidence the real power of God in operation. He knows if he can prejudice people against all physical manifestations, he has robbed them of all they would have received through the operation of the Spirit of God upon their physical beings, and it is when the power of God is operating thus, that the best results are obtained. I have seen this wonderful power cause the lame to rise and walk—made instantly and perfectly whole. I have seen it heal the sick in many cases. While feeling this mighty power operating in my body, I have laid my hands on people in many cases, and they would be filled instantly with the Holy Ghost. All the real work that is done on every line is done by this mighty power, which comes upon us and which at times shakes the body, at other times prostrates us, speaks and sings in tongues, and produces many other manifestations. It is none other than the power of God. It is no less a personage than the Blessed Holy Spirit Himself working among the saints of God. This explains why the devil tries to counterfeit it, and the flesh tries to imitate it. Let all the saints yield themselves to God; hate the flesh; and, above all, give no place to the devil.

Speaking in Tongues Is the Evidence of the Baptism in the Holy Spirit

For six years the question of whether speaking in other tongues as the Spirit gives utterance is the evidence of the baptism in the Holy Spirit, has been much agitated. The real question is, “Do all who receive the gift of the Holy Spirit speak in tongues as at Pentecost, at the time?” Perhaps no point of doctrine has ever been more bitterly contested. It is also doubtful if any other point of doctrine was ever so shamefully compromised, as this one has been by some in the movement. It would be impossible to calculate what the work has suffered, as a result of this point of truth’s being compromised. The work has never suffered from the effects of the opposition of those who stood on the outside of the movement, and bitterly opposed this and other truths. It has suffered from the effects of those who claim to be Pentecostal people, and at the same time deny this great distinguishing truth of the movement.

Now it is not to be supposed that this truth is opposed just simply as an ordinary point of doctrine is opposed. Men in this day, as a rule, are not concerned enough about a small point of doctrine to fight against it, as this doctrine has been fought. This is one of the penetrating truths of God, such as He often sends, that locates every man that hears it. If God did not send His plain, pointed messages and truths into the world occasionally, men would have a much smoother time of it. But just about the time men get settled down to rest in carnal security, on their highly prized but false theories, God sends a plain message of truth, that simply puts every soul on the face of the earth in a corner. In all past time both the message of God and His messengers as well, have been rejected and opposed. By very far the greatest majority of the messengers God has sent to the world have been utterly rejected, and a great per cent of them have been slain.

God’s message puts men under conviction, and, unless they are willing to give heed to it, there is nothing left for them to do but to try to get that which disturbs them out of the way. It has been no exception with this truth. While no one, so far as we know, has been killed for preaching it and for the results that have followed, on every side we have seen it stir up the same spirit that was manifested in those who have murdered the saints and martyrs in the past. We have heard it said over and over again, that our ministers ought to be hung, or killed, or sent to jail. We have been threatened, and heard others threatened. Some have been assaulted and shamefully entreated. The most bitter and scathing articles have been published and circulated against the truth and those who preach it. In a word, there has been a very determined and united effort to exterminate this point of doctrine.

We do not believe that all those who have opposed this doctrine have understood fully what they were doing. We believe that most of them, if they would own the truth, would acknowledge, however, that they hate this truth, because it says to them, in so many words, that they have not the baptism. We believe it is because they are located. Of one thing we feel certain: The devil knows exactly why he hates it and opposes it so. It is because it exposes every false theory that he ever got men to believe. He knows that, if every person he has ever deceived and made satisfied with a theory, and thus robbed of the baptism, should see this truth and tarry for the baptism, they would receive it. He knows that just as soon as men see this truth, they will begin to seek God, and will never be satisfied again till they get the real baptism. He knows just how it stirs men up. He knows this is the one thing that represents the genuine, Scriptural baptism in the Holy Spirit. Therefore he knows the importance of getting it out of the way. He knows that, even among Pentecostal people, as soon as he gets them to lose interest in this great Pentecostal truth, they will settle down, and that in a little while people will quit seeking and receiving the Holy Spirit. One thing one need never be in doubt about; and that is the attitude of the devil toward this truth, or whether he fully understands it.

As small a thing as the speaking in tongues seems to many to be, it is marvelous what a stir it has made in the world. When six years ago it was first preached on the Pacific Coast, that the speaking in tongues was the evidence of the baptism, it met with bitter opposition from the holiness people. The most of the people who heard did not believe it. Therefore they branded it as a false doctrine, and the man that preached it as a false prophet. But some tarried and the Lord met them. In a short time most of those who had opposed were seeking, and most of them received. Then those who had been so confident that they had received the Holy Spirit before, and thus had opposed this teaching, knew two things: first, that they never had had the baptism before; second, that the doctrine that the tongues is the evidence was true.

Right here the line began to be drawn. When the people saw the power of God coming on the people, and heard them speaking in tongues, those, as a rule, who were acknowledged as the most spiritual among them recognized that it was God, and took their stand for it. The other class said they did not believe it was God, continued to oppose, and none of them ever received the baptism. On the other hand those who saw and believed that it was God and became seekers, almost without exception, received the glorious baptism and spoke in tongues. The writer of this article has had this glorious experience for over five years, and has heard all that could be said against it. He gladly places himself on record today as believing, beyond a doubt and without a single misgiving, and more strongly, if possible, than ever before, that this is the genuine, Scriptural baptism in the Spirit, and that in glory and blessing it eclipses all other experiences. No experience is, or could be more valuable except conversion, which is of course the experience on which all other experiences of the Christian life are built. The writer knows today, as he has known from the first, that when the blessed Holy Spirit, the third Person in the Trinity, comes in to take up His permanent abode, He speaks in other tongues.

So far as our knowledge extends, every one that went forth for the first year or two stood firmly for the truth that the tongues are the evidence of the baptism. Wherever they went this simple truth put people in a corner, and either drove them away or started them to seeking. The result was, scores received. The instructions were as simple as they could have been. “Just yield yourself up to the Lord and trust the Blood and wait,” they would say. As souls did this, the Spirit would fall on them. The results were the same in all localities. When the power would come upon people they would often fall helplessly to the floor. Generally they would be shaken more or less violently. This was a trying experience to some who never felt the power before and who of course did not understand it. “Just let Him have His way,” the workers would say, and soon the person who was under the power would begin to speak in tongues.

No person ever had a stranger experience than those who speak in tongues for the first time. No one could ever describe it. To me it was the strangest, most glorious and wonderful experience I had ever had. The power, which has already overcome and which shakes the person’s body, simply moves to his vocal organs and begins to operate on them and, if yielded to, soon produces a language. After a person had spoken in tongues we pronounced him through. By this we meant his baptism was completed. Many would have the power on them and not get through to the baptism at the first time, or even the second. When this was the case the power of God, after dealing with a person, would simply lift from him. When He filled him and spoke in tongues He remained with him. This position we held from the first, and we hold it today. All who are really baptized speak in tongues at the time.

One thing we have observed, and we have been careful to observe all that has happened in this glorious movement. Whenever they cease in any place to teach that the tongues are the evidence the power of God lifts and they have very few baptisms any more. Wherever they stand for this truth and really preach it, if they are straight, or reasonably straight, in other doctrines and are a clean people, the power never leaves them, and people continue to get the baptism. In a word, it is a truth that God has been pleased to honor from the first, and He is honoring it just as much today as ever. God always honors His own message.

Last year I went to a mission where they had gone back on this point of truth. The work was all run down. The place was comparatively empty. In two weeks, as I stood as firm as a rock for this truth and the Finished Work of Calvary, the place was more than crowded. Hundreds were turned away who could not get into the building, and it was a large one. God put people under awful conviction and many were saved. Many who had been saved and even filled with the Spirit came, with tears of repentance, confessed that they were backslidden, and got right with the Lord. In less than three months the Lord baptized over one hundred and fifty in the Holy Spirit. Some try to convince me that it is the messenger that the Lord is honoring. Brethren, I disclaim any such honor. It is the truth of God that He is honoring. God is not putting Himself out in this day, speaking after the manner of men, to honor any man. He is honoring His word and every man who preaches it in its fulness. It is not to be denied that God honors those who live near enough to Him to hear from Him, and to get His message and preach it. God certainly honors those who have honest, true, faithful hearts; but it is saying entirely too much, when we say that it is the man the Lord is honoring with results. When a man gets the message of God and preaches it, God honors both the man and the message. The highest honor that God could confer upon one, in our judgment, is to co-operate with him, and bless his labors, and trust him with His message.

When God sent the message that the tongues were the evidence of the baptism, He accompanied it with His mighty power, which confirmed it. Certainly the man He used to deliver the message was blest and honored of God, as long as he faithfully delivered the message. God gave him success, as men measure success. It was God’s own message, however, that He set His seal upon and confirmed with the signs following. Wherever His message has been faithfully preached from that day to this, His blessing and power accompanies it. It is one message that always brings results. We have never proclaimed it in any place yet, that it did not produce results.

When it is declared that the tongues are the evidence of the baptism, people who have set under the ministry of those who do not believe and preach this point of truth, though they claim to be Pentecostal people, and have never received the Spirit, will get their baptism. During the present Chicago revival, about thirty have come in from one assembly that claims to be a Pentecostal assembly, but does not stand for the tongues’ evidence, and received their baptism. Those who think it is not necessary to preach this truth are robbing the people of the baptism, and themselves of the results they would otherwise see. They are failing to honor God by faithfully proclaiming His message for today. They fail to do their duty to the people by telling them the truth. If they told them the truth, they would know they did not have the baptism, and would get down and wait on God till He baptized them. Every soul who receives the Spirit is always an encouragement to others who are still tarrying, or who may be undecided. People soon lose interest, when they do not see something happening. As soon as seekers see others receiving, it inspires faith in them to believe they will receive also.

God, in the beginning, chose to make this point a pivotal one. He used it to draw the line between those who had the baptism and those who had not. He used it to corner men. He used it to locate all classes of men. It located honest men, who thought they had the baptism and who had not. It located dishonest men, who wanted to pose as having the baptism, and who knew they did not. It located those who were ignorant of the whole matter. Many have come into our meetings and shown unbounded astonishment, when they saw the mighty power of God. They had never seen anything like it before. When they would see it, and hear the saints praising God and magnifying the name of Jesus and the power of His precious Blood, they would be convinced that it was the power of God, and would fall on their knees and receive the Spirit the first service they were in. The truth of God accompanied by the power of God always did and always will locate men. At all times and in all places many have refused to be convinced, no matter what God did. In spite of all the mighty works wrought by Jesus Christ, men found an excuse for rejecting Him. They absolutely refused to be convinced. No doubt every false report they heard, or any so-called excuse that came to them was received with the greatest joy. No doubt they intentionally ignored His mighty works and sniffed at them. Nevertheless, He was the Son of God; and when they, for very envy and jealousy, had condemned Him to death to get Him out of the way, God gloriously raised Him up from the dead. As further proof, God poured out the Spirit before their very eyes, as it were, and let them see His mighty signs and wonders wrought by the hands of those simple followers of Jesus, who received the Holy Spirit and spoke in tongues. Those who could be convinced were convinced. Others still refused to be convinced, hardening their hearts against God, and added this to their sins, that they persecuted and killed the Apostles of Jesus Christ.

So it is in this day. Those whom the truth, accompanied by the power of God, will convince, are being convinced. Others reject both the truth and the power, and thus place themselves in the position of those who fight against God. There is nothing that would convince these people because their hearts are hardened against God. No matter what God did, even though He should raise the dead in their very presence, they would say that it was not the power of God. This was what they did in the days of Jesus, and this is what they will do today.

God chose that this sign should follow, when the Spirit was poured out upon His own Apostles on the day of Pentecost, Acts 2:1–5. It was recognized as an infallible proof at the house of Cornelius, Acts 10:44–47. The church at Jerusalem later, when dealing with the Apostle Peter for going in and eating with the gentiles, at once dropped the case, when they heard the gentiles had received the same Spirit, in exactly the same way they had received Him, that is, accompanied by speaking in other tongues. At Ephesus many years after Pentecost we see the same sign following, Acts 19:6. It is the sign that thousands of the saints are receiving today, when the blessed Spirit comes upon them and fills them and seals them unto the day of redemption. Thank God for restoring this old landmark. It is the sure sign that what we receive is the Bible brand.

3. The Finished Work of Calvary and the Meaning of Sanctification
