Sanctification: Is It a Definite, Second, Instantaneous Work of Grace?

This subject is attracting so much attention in the Pentecostal movement just now, and is being so widely discussed, that it seems necessary to devote some time and space to it. I have received many letters asking questions on the subject, and hundreds of my friends who have heard me preach on the subject have earnestly requested me to deal with the subject more thoroughly in the paper, that others might receive the light and blessing they have received. It might be well for me to state that from my conversion, thirteen years ago, to the present time, I have continually associated with holiness people; and that for years, in my preaching, I referred to sanctification as a second work of grace, bringing several things in my attempt to prove it:

First, that many people, after being converted, had received what seemed to them to be a definite experience.

Second, that the Scriptures clearly taught that there was an experience to be received after conversion. When I referred to the Scriptures I always used the experience of the Apostles at Pentecost and the experience of the Samaritans as recorded in the 8th of Acts; also the account of the Spirit’s falling on Cornelius under Peter’s preaching recorded in Acts 10:44–47, and the account of the outpouring at Ephesus, Acts 19:1–6.

Third, I used the exhortations of Paul in his epistles to the churches as proof that the New Testament assemblies did not have all the Lord had for them. Fourth, I used the condition of the religious world today. I declared that large numbers of them were Christian people, yet their lives proved that they were not sanctified. They did not live it. Some of my teaching was that in justification we are pardoned; in sanctification we are cleansed; that in justification the tree is cut down; that in sanctification the stump is taken out; that in justification we are saved from evil deeds and habits; that in sanctification we are cleansed from evil tempers and principles; that in justification we are saved from what we have done; that in sanctification we are saved from what we are.

To prove that it was a definite, instantaneous work, I referred to the statements of scholars, viz.: that the references to sanctification in the original Greek are in the aorist tense, which denotes completed action in the indefinite past. This is only a very condensed statement of what I believed and taught on the subject, as I was perfectly familiar with every theory commonly taught by any of the leading holiness teachers and writers. I had heard most of their leading preachers, and had read volume after volume on the subject by their leading writers. It is only fair to myself to state, however, that I always found very great difficulty in harmonizing the definite second work theory with the plain teaching of the Word. I had no trouble, however, in proving that the Bible taught entire sanctification. It seems to me no one could believe the Bible and attempt to deny that its standard of teaching is Holiness unto the Lord. But the minds of some have become so biased by the erroneous second work theory, that you can state clearly to them that you do believe in entire sanctification and that the Bible teaches it as God’s only standard and that therefore no one can be justified short of it, and while still claiming their second work experience, they will go away and say that you do not believe in sanctification.

I believe the time has come that God wants His people to understand His Word, and to accept it in preference to any theory. From the day the Holy Spirit fell on me and filled me I could never preach the second work theory again. I must say that in theory I still held to it, but was restrained in the Spirit from preaching it any more. From the first, the Spirit dealt with me and revealed clearly in my heart the plain Bible truth of the finished work of the Cross of Calvary; but it took months for me to get it clear enough in my mind to be willing to entirely discard the old theory, and take my stand on the simple living truth of God. I moved with great care out of respect for the many recognized great men, including Wesley, who had taught sanctification as a second work of grace. I waited until I was sure that there was no possibility of my being mistaken on the subject from a Scriptural standpoint. Then, in the fear of the Lord, I preached the finished work of Calvary—one work of grace. From the first, God wonderfully honored it and the Spirit fell in power wherever it was preached.

I have preached on this subject to thousands of people since then. I honestly believe that ninety-nine out of every one hundred of them have accepted it. Not one has ever come and told me that what I preached was not the Bible. Some who did not see it at first have said, “Yes, what you preach is the Scripture, but I am going to search the Scriptures to see if I cannot find another work taught somewhere.” I say humbly, not one has ever come to point out the other work to me in the Bible.

The plain teaching of the Word of God is identification with Jesus Christ. The thought of God concerning our salvation is expressed in a death, a burial, and a resurrection. Our faith in God’s plan is clearly expressed in the ordinance of baptism. We believe that we are dead with Christ, therefore we are buried with Him; and if we have been planted together in the likeness of His death, we believe that we shall be also in the likeness of His resurrection. Romans 6:6 says that our “old man” was crucified with Christ, that the body of sin might be done away. The seventh verse says, “For he that hath died is justified from sin.” Col. 2:11–13 says, “In whom ye were also circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands, in the putting off of the body of the flesh in the circumcision of Christ; having been buried with Him in baptism, wherein ye were also raised with Him through faith in the working of God, who raised Him from the dead. And you being dead through your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, you did He make alive together with Him, having forgiven us all our trespasses.”

Please notice that the body of the flesh is put off in the circumcision of Christ. Please notice in the twelfth verse, that we were buried with Him in baptism and raised with Him through faith in the working of God. Please also notice in the thirteenth verse, that we are made alive together with Christ. The first verse of the Third Chapter of Colossians tells us “we are risen with Christ.” The third verse says, “For ye died, and your life is hid with Christ in God.”

Now all the teaching of the second work people has to do with the destruction or removal of the “old man.” They teach that a saved person has a dual nature. That while we are made a new creature, yet the “old man” is in us, and that he (the Adamic nature) is removed in the second work of grace.

Now as soon as it is established that the “old man” is crucified and slain in conversion, the whole foundation from under their theory is entirely removed, and their structure tumbles to the ground; yet the plain teaching in all the Scripture is to the effect, that the “old man” was crucified with Christ, and that we are justified on the ground that Jesus Christ took our place and died in our stead. Now, why was it necessary for Jesus Christ to die for us? Because the sentence of death pronounced upon Adam the first, the “old man,” was handed down to us and must be executed before we could be justified. So when Jesus Christ went to the Cross He not only took our sins upon Him, but He, in the fullest sense, became our Substitute and took our place, and the sentence of death which hung over us was executed in Him; or, in other words, our “old man,” the Adamic nature, was crucified with Christ that it might be destroyed or done away.

Now, when a penitent sinner is made to see that Jesus Christ died in His stead, his living faith identifies him with Christ in His death. From that moment, from God’s point of view, or, as some say, in the eyes of the law, he is dead. He has died in the person of his Substitute, Jesus Christ. He is now a candidate for baptism; that is, to be buried with Christ by baptism into death, because his faith has identified him with Christ in His death on the Cross. But God has quickened him in Christ, when he believed in Jesus Christ, and he passes out of death into life, being made a new creature in Christ. So, just as Christ came forth from the grave to die no more, the believer in Christ comes up from his burial in water to die no more, but rather to be identified with Jesus Christ in his new life. There is no other ground on which people are buried except death; neither is there any excuse for burying any one in water except that he is dead with Christ; and every student of the Bible will agree with me that it was the “old man” that died and that the believer is supposed to rise to walk in newness of life.

This, then, will make baptism (the watery grave) the dividing line between the old life and the new. In the old life the “old man” (the flesh) ruled. In the new life the Spirit of God, Who, from a Bible standpoint, is supposed to be received immediately following baptism, is supposed to rule. Symbolically the “old man” is supposed to cling to us up to the time of our baptism, but to be buried there, never to rise again. The Old Testament type of this is found in the Book of Exodus, where God delivered His people from the bondage of Pharaoh, who is a type of the “old man.” When God purposed to smite the first born of Egypt, He commanded Israel, through Moses, to kill a lamb and sprinkle its blood upon the door-posts and upon the lintel of the door, saying, “When I see the blood, I will pass over you.” That night God smote the first born of all Egypt, but His own people were saved through the blood of a slain lamb. This, then, brought them under the blood, but they were not yet free from the “old man.” Next, we see them on the banks of the Red Sea, whose waters divided, and into which they entered, followed by the “old man.” God’s promise to them was, that they should never see these Egyptians again. Next, we see Israel, God’s people, who are redeemed by the blood of a slain lamb, come up from the waters onto the dry land; but the “old man” who had followed them to and into the waters was overthrown in the midst of the sea, and left in the very bottom of the middle of the sea, while God’s redeemed people on the shores of deliverance, sang unto the Lord the song of redemption, forever free from the bondage of the “old man.” This is a most beautiful type of God’s simple plan of salvation through the precious Blood of Jesus Christ. Pages could be written giving Scriptures to prove our position, but we feel that we must take up and deal with the other side of the question.

As stated above, no one has yet come to us with the Scripture that establishes sanctification as a second work of grace. They come with their experience at times. They also speak of the condition of the religious world, which they say we must acknowledge to be in a justified state. They also point to the condition of the New Testament Churches, and the exhortations to holiness in the Epistles.

Concerning experiences, we would say that we doubt not that many people come into conscious possession of the experience of sanctification after conversion; but because they were not taught the truth in the first place, shall we teach all others that they must seek sanctification as a second work? I know that when God saved me, He fully saved me. What should have been taught me, was to receive the Holy Ghost and present myself to God as alive from the dead and to reckon, in living faith, myself dead. Had I done this, I should never have had any trouble. As it was, having no teaching or help, and not having received the Holy Ghost, I walked in a heavenly state for several months and then grew cold. When I applied to the teachers for help, they told me, in all honesty, no doubt, that what I needed was sanctification. What they should have told me was that I was partially backslidden, that I had lost the joy out of my experience, and needed to get back under the Blood, where I was in the first place. Their failing to do this caused me two years of struggling and grief. Then God in His mercy brought me back to the foot of the Cross, where the precious Blood flows; and to my indescribable joy, I found myself in possession of the same sweet, rich experience that I had at first, but was so full of the second-work theory, that I called it a second work of grace. I believe thousands of honest souls have done the very same thing. I further believe that large numbers of people, if they told the truth, would have to say that they have passed through numbers of such experiences as I have mentioned, that time and time again they have wandered from God, and lost the joy of their salvation, and had to humble their hearts and seek His precious face, until they stood again at the foot of the Cross where the precious Blood flows. To those who say they have had two experiences, I would say, I have had more than two, and almost every saint of God that I have talked with has told me that they, too, have had more than two experiences. To them the final experience would be the definite one, and it might be a fifth, or tenth, just as clear as any person’s second, while the plain truth is, that only one is necessary if we know and obey the truth.

As stated above, some do not know, at first, enough of the truth to get the joy that they would receive, did they possess a knowledge of the truth. Therefore, with new light on what they have in Christ, comes new blessing.

As to the condition of the religious world, while we know many of them have at some time been saved, we further know that large numbers of them have never been born again. The low state of grace seen among believers is no proof whatever that sanctification is a second work of grace. All honest people will have to admit that the majority of the people in the so-called churches are not justified. It is not a second work of grace they need. They need to repent and get right with God. And in hundreds of cases, that have come under my observation, as soon as they repent and get right with God, they get the baptism in the Holy Spirit, just as we have seen hundreds of sinners, who had never heard of a second work of grace, do as soon as they were converted. As to the Scriptures: the Apostles and those at Samaria, and those at the house of Cornelius, and those at Ephesus, did receive something definite after they were converted; but it was not sanctification. It was the glorious gift of the Holy Ghost, Who is the seal of our complete salvation in Jesus Christ, Who announces Himself by speaking in tongues. All Pentecostal people know that these wonderful experiences in Acts have no reference to sanctification as a second work of grace, but exclusively to receiving the gift of the Holy Ghost. All others ought to know it.

As to the teaching of the Epistles, every Bible scholar knows, or should know, that the Epistles were written to people who were not only saved and sanctified in Jesus Christ, but were filled with the Holy Ghost, and these Assemblies abounded in gifts of the Holy Spirit. Romans 12:1 is often used as a proof that Paul was trying to get the Roman Church sanctified, but we must remember that the Romans were not only saved but filled with the Spirit, and that Romans 12:4–8 makes it clear that the Spirit had distributed the gifts to them. Thus Paul’s exhortation to them was to present their bodies a living sacrifice, or, in other words, to yield themselves up wholly to God to do His will in all things, which would mean for them to be a continual sacrifice.

Much has been said and written, especially by the opposers of the Pentecostal work, of the condition of the Corinthian Church. They are declared to be an unsanctified church. The advocates of the second work theory say that Paul was trying to get them sanctified; but is this true? Let us test it by the Word. 1 Cor. 1:2 says, they are the Church of God—sanctified in Christ Jesus, called saints (holy ones). In the fourth verse, Paul thanks God for the grace which was given them in Christ. In the fifth verse he says, “In everything ye were enriched in Him, in all utterance and all knowledge.” In the sixth verse he says, “The testimony of Christ was confirmed in you”; in the seventh verse he says, “Ye come behind in no gift; waiting for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Who dare say that this Church had never been sanctified? This is the best record given of any Church in the New Testament. They were enriched in everything, gloriously filled with the Holy Ghost, and every gift of the Spirit was in operation in their midst. One man among them, however, had fallen into awful sin. When Paul’s letter was received he was overcome with grief, truly repented, and was restored. Some others had allowed a spirit of partiality or favoritism to get in, even going so far as to contend about Paul, Apollos, Cephas, Christ, etc., etc. For this the Apostle reproved them. We have seen this thing among every order of holiness people. Some holiness people contend they are of Booth, some that they are of Caradine, some they are of Godbey, some they are of Wesley, etc., etc. None of them seem to think it is a proof that they are not sanctified; but they think it was a proof that the Corinthians were not sanctified.

Again, the condition of the Galatian Church is held up as a sure proof that they were not sanctified, and that Paul was trying to get them sanctified as a definite, second work of grace. But is it true? Let us see what Paul says of them. In the first chapter, sixth verse, he says, “That you are so quickly removing from Him that called you into the Grace of Christ, unto a different Gospel.” In the eighth verse he says, “But though we, or an angel from Heaven, should preach unto you another Gospel other than that which we preached unto you, let him be anathema.” In Chapter 3:1 he says, “O foolish Galatians, who did bewitch you, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was openly set forth crucified;” and in the second verse he says, “This only would I learn from you: Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?” In verse three, he says, “Are ye so foolish, having begun in the Spirit, are ye now perfected in the flesh?” Nothing could be clearer. They had received Jesus Christ. 1 Cor. 1:30 says, “He of God is made unto us Wisdom, Righteousness, Sanctification and Redemption.” They had received the Holy Spirit. They had begun in the Spirit, but were going back into the flesh. Their danger was in departing from the plain way of faith, wherein they had started, and going back to the law, thus coming into bondage. Paul’s plain exhortation to them is to return to the simple Gospel of faith which he preached to them, and to have nothing to do with the law; to walk in the Spirit, and not in the flesh. All Pentecostal people, I am sure, will agree with me in this.

I have heard some claim that Ephesians 3:14–20 was a prayer for the sanctification of the Ephesians. In the light of truth this statement is ridiculous from every point of view. In the first place, we are taught in the 19th of Acts, sixth verse, that the charter members of the Ephesian Assembly, numbering twelve, were filled with the Holy Ghost, and spoke in tongues and prophesied. In the 13th verse of the first chapter of Paul’s Epistle to the Ephesians, he tells them that, having believed, they were “sealed in the Holy Spirit of promise, which is an earnest of our inheritance unto the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of His glory.” In Chapter 4:30, he warns them not to grieve the Holy Spirit of God, whereby we are sealed unto the day of redemption. This is proof positive that the Ephesians were not only saved and sanctified in Jesus Christ, but filled with the Holy Ghost, and sealed unto the day of redemption. In Acts 20:31, Paul reminds the elders of the Assembly at Ephesus that by the space of three years he had ceased not to admonish every one night and day with tears. I wonder if anybody really believes that the Apostle Paul would dwell for three whole years among a people laboring night and day among them, and leave them in a converted state, but not sanctified.

One more statement I will make: while, as repeatedly stated in this article, I recognize the exhortations of the Apostle to the Assemblies, to live a holy, separate life because they are dead in Christ and living in Him, there is not one recorded instance in the New Testament where any one was dealt with after conversion to lead them into the experience of sanctification. No one can produce a single instance. When men believed, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus; the hands of the Apostles were laid on them, and they were filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke in tongues; and were then carefully instructed how they ought to live in this world and to please God. Were I to write to holiness and Pentecostal people, after all I have seen in many years dwelling among them, I could point to many errors that needed correcting, and would feel constrained to earnestly exhort all of them to yield themselves more fully to God and to the control of the Holy Spirit, that the greater blessing and power of God might rest upon them.

As lengthy as this article is, it has not begun to cover the ground, but very many lovers of truth will see the truth of it. Some of them will look into the Bible and decide not to preach the old theory again, unless they can find Scripture to prove it; a few will say, I cannot accept this because it is not according to my experience; a few others will say, it is contrary to what Wesley taught or to what some other man has taught. The last two classes will pay little or no attention to what the Scriptures teach; some of them, to prove their narrowness and bigotry, will say, as I have heard of a few saying before, that the writer has gone back on sanctification. The writer is wholly sanctified to God in Christ. He holds his experience in living faith. He believes sanctification is God’s only standard. He is filled with the Holy Spirit, with the Scriptural signs following, and is so deeply in love with the truth that he is willing to suffer for it if necessary. The Word of God and the Spirit of God have led him to the belief set forth in this article; namely, that he believes in the finished work of the Cross of Calvary. He believes that a sinner receives Jesus Christ, and that a believer receives the Holy Ghost. These two experiences he finds clearly taught in the New Testament—he fails to find any other. Let us search for the truth, and receive it when we find it.

The Finished Work of Calvary: It Makes Plain the Great Work of Redemption

The confusion and misunderstanding in the religious world today is largely due to the fact that the simple Gospel of Christ is not taught and understood. Christ’s great work of redemption is the sure foundation on which real Christianity rests. “Other foundation can no man lay than is laid which is Jesus Christ.” If the great work of redemption and atonement wrought by Christ on the Cross of Calvary is left out, it is hard to see that Christianity is very far superior to some other religions. Satan knows this, and is leaving no stone unturned in his unceasing effort to blind the eyes of the people to this great fact. It is a fact that cannot be denied, that he has very largely succeeded in doing so. Only a remnant remain who see and cling to Christ as their personal Savior and Redeemer.

The surest possible way to overturn a building is to remove its foundation. The basic truths of the Gospel are that Christ became a substitute for sinners and died in their stead, and that men are saved by faith in Him. If this teaching be not true, then the whole Gospel or Christian structure is built upon an absolutely false foundation, Christ was a false teacher and an impostor and all who have trusted in Him are lost. The time has come that God will have the truth go forth and men will be called to decide one way or the other. God will have His simple, primitive Gospel preached in all the world exactly as it was in the days of the Apostles, so that all men can decide whether they wish to stand for Christ and His Gospel or for the foolish theories of men.

This makes the battle to largely center around the glorious truth of the “Finished Work of Christ on Calvary,” which is the most glorious and powerful truth of the Gospel. Yea, it is the very center and heart of the Gospel. When once this truth is established it clearly draws the line so that no one need be mistaken as to where he is. Thousands of people, who are trusting in morality, legality, philanthropy, humanitarianism, church membership, the brotherhood of man and the hundreds of other silly things in which men are being made to trust by false teachers who are influenced by the devil, will have their eyes opened to the fact that if the Gospel is true, all these things combined could never save a single soul. And all will be made to know that if any or all other things combined could ever save even one soul, then the Gospel is not true and Christ is dead in vain. In this decade the Gospel will be proven true. It will be confirmed by the signs that follow it. The establishment of the truth of the Gospel will explode every theory of men in existence concerning the salvation of lost men.

Many who are in the Spirit see clearly the great battleground and the point at issue. When the truth of the “Finished Work of Christ” was first sounded forth through Pentecostal Testimony, a large number saw what a conflict it would cause. None saw it clearer than the editor who wrote the articles on the subject. How could it be otherwise? The Finished Work is by far the most important teaching in the Bible. What could we expect but that the enemy would oppose with all his power? One brother after another was convinced by the Word of God itself. Nothing else could have convinced them, as they had had the other thing drilled into them for years, and like myself, well knew that it would mean the loss of friendship of all who did not see it, and who would still cling to the second work theory. One after another under challenge said, “I will find it in the Word of God, and convince Durham that he is wrong.” They would then begin the most careful search of the Scriptures and after days would be compelled to acknowledge to themselves and others that they could not find sanctification taught as a second definite work of grace in the New Testament, nor anywhere else, as to that. Then they would write and ask our forgiveness for having opposed us, and inform us that they had taken their stand for the Finished Work.

Some have tried to make it appear that people have simply accepted my teaching without investigation. Nothing could be further from the truth. No truth which I ever presented has ever been so carefully investigated as this one. Many have been forced to acknowledge that they could not find their theory taught in the Scripture; long before they would accept the truth. Others have declared they would never go back on some experience they had, no difference what the Bible taught. By far the greater number of all who have heard this teaching, however, have accepted it; however prejudiced they may have been against the truth and those who preached it. In fact it is a truth that is so clear and convincing that once one’s attention is called to it he cannot help but see it unless he simply closes his eyes and turns away.

The doctrine of the Finished Work, brings us back to the simple plan of salvation. Christ died for us. He became a substitute for everyone of us; for He tasted death for every man. Here is a truth so simple and yet so great that it is wonderful. We are not saved simply because we are forgiven our sins. We are saved through identification with our Savior Substitute, Jesus Christ. We are given life because He died for us and rose again. But some one may ask, “How do we become identified with our Substitute?” We answer, “By faith alone.” We are condemned and sentenced to death. Christ, the Blessed Son of God, stepped in and took our place and died in our stead, thus paying the death penalty that we might go free. When the truth is preached and we tremblingly fall at His feet and cry out, “What must I do?” the word comes back “Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved.” This does not, as we have been taught, mean that we shall be partly saved by having our outward sins forgiven. This would not be salvation. Salvation is an inward work. It means a change of heart. It means a change of nature. It means that old things pass away and that all things become new. It means that all condemnation and guilt is removed. It means that the old man, or old nature, which was sinful and depraved and which was the very thing in us that was condemned, is crucified with Christ. This makes Christ all in all as Savior, and faith the only means by which we can become identified with Him.

How different are the theories preached today, compared with the Gospel preached by the Apostles. On every side men are telling us today that there is no saving virtue or merit in the Blood of Christ, but that He was a very great teacher, and that He was our example of a perfect man. They deny that we are saved through the merits of His precious blood, and set at nought His blessed work of redemption. They deny His Deity and make him a mere man. They tell us the world needs a religion of love. One that recognizes the brotherhood of all men, and that there is good in all religion. Thus they rob us of our Blessed Redeemer. They entirely rob us of the Gospel of Christ which the Apostles preached and which we find in the Bible. No religion ever taught or advocated by anyone could ever teach and enjoin more love and good works than the religion of Christ. The point is that we are not taught that we are saved by these things. Imagine, if you can, one of the Apostles going forth preaching and telling men that they were to believe that Jesus was a great and good man, and that this coupled with good works would save them. A thousand times no! They declared that He was the Son of God, and that God had raised Him up from the dead. They declare that He died for our sins and that we were saved by grace through faith. They made everything to center in Christ, declaring Him to be our only hope. They exhorted to a clean, separate, holy life, fruitful in every good work, separate from the world, lived in fellowship with God, not as a means of being saved, but as a sure proof of salvation already received by faith in Christ. It has remained for modern theorists to rob the Son of God of His title of World’s Redeemer, and thus of His right to the title of Savior, leaving Him a mere man.

So persistent has been the work of Satan along the line of deceiving the people, and blinding their eyes so that they would not see the great truth concerning the sacrifice of Christ on Calvary, that, not only have the eyes of the people of the world been blinded, but a large percent of those in the churches as well. People have been made to look to so many other things that Christ has largely been lost sight of. They have turned to theories and creeds, experiences, blessings, works of grace, states of feeling, standings in churches, acceptance of certain truths, and so many other things that their vision of the Blessed Christ of Calvary has been dimmed. God has sent the Blessed Holy Spirit to His Children in these last days, to witness clearly in their hearts that the Gospel of Christ, as contained in the Scripture, is true. Men, doctrines, experiences and churches have been exalted in the earth for centuries. In the end of the age the Holy Spirit has come to exalt Jesus Christ, and give Him His rightful place in the hearts and lives of all God’s children, as well as in the assembly. Never has such a fight been made for men and the things of men as is being made in these days. These are days that try men’s souls. These are days when God is sifting and bringing to light. These are days when the theories of men are being tried by the Word of God, and shown up in their true light. They are weighed in the balance and found wanting. Men are proving their loyalty to their theories and their disloyalty to God, by clinging to their old theories after they are exposed by the Scriptures. They are in many instances fighting the truth of God with all their power. Most of them are not even attempting to bring Scripture to prove their position. They have none to bring; so they try to stop the progress of truth by denouncing those who bring the truth. This method of warfare is sure to fail. What God undertakes, He does. He has undertaken to establish the truth concerning the Finished Work of Christ and the baptism in the Holy Spirit, and He will certainly do it. No power will ever prevent His doing so.

One thing is sure, and all would do well to recognize it. Time can never change nor interfere with the plan of God. The Gospel of Jesus Christ is exactly the same today that it was in the beginning. A man is saved today on exactly the same terms he was in the days of the Apostles. Men change, customs change, churches change, very greatly, both as to their faith and practice, but the Gospel of Christ and God’s plan of salvation remain exactly as they were in the beginning. If Jesus Christ ever was the Redeemer of mankind He is such today. If man ever needed redemption he needs it today. If repentance and faith were necessary in the days of the Apostles they are necessary today. Not in even one place in the New Testament is it ever taught that there is any other way of salvation except through Jesus Christ. Over and over again it is declared that there is no other way, no name except His great name that has salvation in it. The same thing is true today. Millions are deceived by the devil into believing that they will be saved in some other way, only to wake up in the end to see that in rejecting Jesus Christ and setting at naught God’s plan, they sealed their own doom and missed the glories of eternal life.

No doubt the second work of grace theory has done more to blind the eyes of people to the simple truth of the Gospel than any other one theory that was ever taught. It has come to thousands of truly saved people declaring that they are not saved, and that, instead of men coming into Christ and receiving eternal life in conversion, all they get is pardon of their outward transgressions. They are told that when God pardoned them He left them full of sin and corruption, and that it requires a second work of grace to save them from hell. Bishop Horner, in his book “The Root,” makes the astounding statement that a converted person has enough sin in him to damn a nation. Of course, if this loathsome doctrine were true, no man is saved till he receives a second work of grace. If the Word of God taught any such thing we would heartily sanction it, and declare to all that unless they had had the second work of grace they were just as much on the way to hell as they ever were. Such teaching is so unscriptural, unreasonable and damaging that by the grace of God we will show it up in its true light, regardless of the way its adherents rage against us. Let them come forward and defend this thing with the Scripture. God’s Word makes it plain that when God saves a man He cleanses him. A saved man is saved no matter what the theorists say. He is saved from sin, death and hell, is a real child of God, possesses eternal life, does not need another work of grace, but needs to abide in Christ, receive and walk in the Spirit, hold fast the faith, grow in grace and in the knowledge of God and of Christ.

The simple truth is that a sinner is identified with Adam. A believer is identified with Jesus Christ. No man is identified with Adam the first and Adam the second at the same time. A sinner is in Adam and Adam is in a sinner. A believer is in Christ and Christ is in a believer. A sinner is condemned in Adam. A believer is free from condemnation in Christ. A sinner has condemnation and a believer has peace. A man is not in Adam and Christ at the same time. Christ and Adam are not in a man at the same time. When Adam fell the old creation was dragged down with him. When Christ arose from the dead, the new creation came up with Him. A sinner is in the kingdom of darkness and sin. A believer is in the kingdom of Jesus Christ. Before conversion a man is in “nature’s darkness.” In conversion he is translated out of nature’s darkness into the Kingdom of God’s dear Son. It is in conversion that a man receives Jesus Christ, the glorious Son of God, and is made a new creature in Him, and old things pass away and all things become new. As these glorious truths grip our souls they put real strength in us, and we become established in our Blessed Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. These are the real truths of the Gospel. The Spirit witnesses to them when they are preached. The signs follow when this Gospel is preached.

Last year while preaching this glorious Gospel and being opposed in every possible way, we saw over four hundred precious souls receive the Blessed Holy Spirit with the speaking in tongues. In a little more than three months of this year we have seen more than two hundred receive the Spirit and speak in tongues. The demand for this wonderful Gospel has increased, till it will be impossible for us to ever go to one place in fifty which send calls. What is the secret of it? It is the real Apostolic Gospel, and the Spirit in God’s people witnesses to it. It is wonderful how God is establishing His people and uniting them. On the other hand, we have carefully observed for more than a year, and we have not seen anything like a revival among those who oppose the “Finished Work” and stand for the second work theory. We have known of very few receiving the baptism among them in any place that we have been. God is confirming His Word with the signs following, and He will not confirm or honor the theories of those who oppose His blessed Truth. Glory to God! Again the world is ringing with the cry of the Gospel heralds who are declaring the same glad message that the Apostles bore. God has freed us from many theories, and restored His glorious truth to us concerning the simple plan of salvation, and with joy we are passing it along. Christ is all in all. With us He shall be given His proper place. The pages of Pentecostal Testimony shall ever be filled with the glorious truth of the Gospel of Jesus Christ the Son of God. Will all lovers of truth pray that God will help us in this great warfare against error and in defense of His Truth?

Some Other Phases of Sanctification

We feel that in order to make ourselves clearly understood by those who never held to the theory that sanctification is a second definite work of grace whereby the heart is cleansed from original sin, but who have understood it to mean a setting apart for a holy use or for some particular order of service, we ought to clearly state our position with regard to this side of the subject.

A few years ago, after receiving the Holy Spirit, He began to open the Word of God to me and to show me the error I was in with regard to the second work of grace as taught by the holiness people and a large per cent of the Pentecostal people. Generally speaking among all holiness people with whom I had mingled (and I had mingled with most orders of them for about nine years), the word sanctify had only one meaning placed upon it. It was invariably interpreted to mean the “second blessing,” the removal of “inbred sin” or the “old man.” We were told that it meant an inward cleansing from the depraved, fallen, or “Adamic nature.” We were told that the terms in Scripture, “old man,” “carnal mind,” “flesh,” “superfluity of naughtiness,” and all kindred terms meant one and the same thing, that they referred to the inward condition of a man in a natural state, and were left in a man when he was converted, and only removed by a second, definite, instantaneous work of grace. This work of grace, they told us, was sanctification and that only those who were sanctified as a second work of grace were sanctified at all. To the terms mentioned above, referring to the depraved nature of man, they added many others, some of which follow: “Inbred corruption,” “the bent to sinning,” “inherited tendency to evil,” “the hydra-headed monster,” “the roots of bitterness,” “the stump of the tree of sin,” “a nest of vipers,” and many other things which it is unnecessary to mention here. Now the question is not whether these terms are correct. I believe those which are quoted from Scripture at least generally do refer to the nature of sin; but the question is, whether a real saved man who is really born again has all this left in him. We were taught, and some are still teaching, that when Paul exhorted to holiness or prayed for the entire sanctification of any person or church, he meant that that person or church had all the things mentioned above in him or it, as the case may be, and that they were to seek for and receive a second work of grace which would instantly remove all this, and leave those who received it with a clean heart. The theory was that justification was the first work of grace and that it removed all outward sins and uncleanness, but the heart was left full of sin and corruption.

When I saw the absurdity of such teaching, so far as it refers to cleansing the heart from sin, I began to write and speak against the doctrine that it takes two works of grace to save and cleanse a man. I denied and still deny that God does not deal with the nature of sin in conversion. I deny that a man who is converted or born again is outwardly washed and cleansed and his heart left unclean with enmity against God in it. I do not believe a man is saved who has that in his heart which the holiness people claim all saved people have in them. How could he be? How can a man be saved and at the same time have “enough sin in him to damn a nation,” as Bishop Horner, in his book “The Root,” says a saved man has in him? Undoubtedly if he has enough in him to damn a nation it would damn him!

Against this teaching we array the plain Scriptural doctrine, that a man is renewed in conversion. We hold that, not only has Christ paid the penalty for our having broken the law, but that He took our place, as descendants of Adam, who share the condemnation and sentence of death pronounced upon him, and died in our stead. When Jesus Christ died, He paid the whole penalty for sin, both committed and original. By one great offering He completed the work of our redemption. In this great work He became a substitute for us. When we believe on Him and accept Him as our Savior, we become identified with Him, and thus saved from all sin. Therefore, through our identification with Him, Who is our Savior and Sanctifier, we are both saved and sanctified. He becomes, or is made, unto us Sanctification. This sanctification, however, has only to do with our cleansing and purification. It is true we are separated unto God in Christ and set apart in Him, for all who come into Him have this blessed experience.

So far in our writings we have generally only dealt with the above phases of sanctification. We have been writing with the Wesleyan, or rather modern holiness people’s, idea of sanctification in our mind. We have been meeting the contentions of those who hold that we are not cleansed till we receive cleansing as a second work of grace.

There is another side, however, to sanctification. In fact, the words sanctify, holy, etc., either in the Old or New Testament, seldom have any reference to cleansing from sin. The word is used of God and angels. It is used of men, vessels, houses, garments worn by the priest, things to be eaten by the priest and their families and assistants, of the city of Jerusalem and different other things. These things, or at least the most of them, never had or needed any work of grace. Most of them were, and could only be, holy by virtue of their office or relationship to God. They were dedicated to His service, set apart for a holy use. A priest was separated from among the people. He was consecrated or dedicated to the service of God.

It is our opinion that every man who filled the office of priest was supposed to be a clean, pure man before he was accepted for the office, and we doubt if he was any holier from the standpoint of purity of heart, after he was consecrated to the office, than he was before. So it was with the vessels of the temple. They were no more holy within themselves, after being consecrated to the service of God, than they were before. After consecration they were holy, sacred or pure by virtue of their relationship to God. So it was with the garments and food of the priest. They were consecrated or dedicated to the holy service of a most holy God. If a priest touched anything which defiled him, he had to go through the forms of purification. These forms consisted of outward washings. It was the same with any of the holy things used in the temple worship and service. If by any means they were even slightly polluted and defiled, they had to undergo a radical cleansing.

Pages might be written to show that sanctification in Scripture does not, and generally could not mean a second, or any other work of grace, but it seems to us this is not necessary. But some contend, “Sanctify means to make holy.” We know that this is one of the meanings of the word, but in most cases in the Scripture the person or thing is made holy by being brought into a certain relationship to God.

Because of our position against the second work theory, and our statement two years ago, that God’s one standard is entire sanctification, some of our friends have, without cause, been afraid that our position did not admit of the belief, that God sets people apart for His holy service after conversion, and in this way sanctifies them. Others, just a few, however, have feared that we did not believe in growth after conversion. Let us repeat that any such fears have been entirely ungrounded. Every such fear will at once vanish, when it is understood that we wrote only concerning cleansing. We believed then, as now, that when God saves a man He fully saves him. We believe He cleanses him from all sin. We believe, however, that this only brings one into a state of spiritual babyhood, and that the whole Christian life with its variety of experiences lies before him. We further believe that the personal conduct of such a one will have a great deal to do with what he develops into, or is chosen for in his Christian life. Many failing to live a holy, separate life before God and the world, do not qualify for any of the honors God has to confer upon those who do walk before Him in perfect obedience.

When God has a great work to do or office to fill, He lays His hand on some one who is already walking before him in holiness or purity of heart and life, and sets him apart for that office or work. This, in Scripture, is called “sanctification.” Even before the foundation of the world, Christ was chosen for the great and holy office of World’s Redeemer. He Himself says of Himself that the Father sanctified Him and sent Him into the world (John 10:36). No one will attempt to claim that this has any reference to cleansing. After twice declaring that His Apostles were clean, and adding that they are not of the world even as He is not of the world, He prays in John 17:17 that the Father will sanctify them, of course meaning to set them apart for the great work they were to do, and offices they were to fill. Proceeding, He says, “For their sakes I sanctify myself.” The Father had sanctified Him and sent Him into the world; now He was to sanctify Himself. He was going to voluntarily set Himself apart, or dedicate Himself for His great work on the Cross. No one could be more pure and holy than He was in every sense of the word. It was His perfection, in the very fullest sense of the word, that qualified Him for the great work He came to do. It required a perfect, spotless being for the great sacrifice for the sins of the world. Christ was sanctified or set apart for this work.

God in conversion brings a man into Christ and makes him holy by washing away all his sins, inward and outward, and giving him a new, clean heart, thus making a new creature of him. The next thing God does for those who are saved, if they trust Him for it, is to fill them with the Holy Spirit. Those thus saved and filled constitute the body, or church of Christ. God expects them to live a clean, holy, separate life, to crucify the flesh, and walk in the Spirit. From those who are faithful in this experience, God chooses those who are to do His work and declare His message in the world. There are many offices to fill in the Church of God, and they can only be filled by those who are cleansed from sin and filled with the Spirit. So, when God wants a man to fill an office in His church, to do a work for Him, He calls one whom He knows to be qualified to fill that office, or do that work. If He calls a man to fill a position in a local assembly, the man is consecrated to the ministry, and set apart, or sanctified to the service of the Lord in the ministry. The same man, if he proves faithful, may be chosen and set apart as a pastor, then as an evangelist, and finally might be called of God to consecrate himself to go as a foreign missionary. The man was sanctified when he was saved, and he is sanctified several times afterward by being set apart for the holy service of God; but at the end he may not be a particle more saved or cleansed than he was to start with. We believe that God calls men after they are saved, that He sets them apart for different lines of ministry and orders of service; but we do not believe that the Word of God teaches that sanctification is a second, definite work of grace, and that it is essential to the cleansing of the heart, and that only those who have had two works of grace are clean.

We know that after conversion, and even after receiving the Holy Spirit, men grievously fail God, and even commit sin, and have to repent and trust the Blood for cleansing. We do know that most people are not living up to their privilege before God, and living the holy, separate life in the Spirit they should, but we know that those who claim two works of grace are just as far below the standard as others. This convinces us that the lack is not so much of some definite experience, as of living the life.

We believe that as long as we live in this world we are in our humanity, and that instead of God’s destroying our human nature, He expects us to control it. In other words, after cleansing us and filling us with the Spirit, He expects us to so yield ourselves to the Holy Spirit continually, that He will have full control of all our faculties. God makes use of our consecrated faculties, when we remain yielded to Him.

We have been wrongfully accused of teaching that we believe people get all there is in conversion, that, therefore, there is no more to look forward to. On the contrary, we believe that God chooses and sets apart only those who are fully saved. We believe that He generally, wonderfully deepens into Himself those whom He chooses. We believe He generally gives them a mightier anointing of His Spirit and power. He gives them a deeper revelation of Christ and His finished Work of redemption on Calvary’s Cross. He often gives some powerful gift or enablement for service. He always equips those He sends forth; but we do not believe it is Scriptural to say that any of these things is a second work of grace. We do not believe in any second work of grace any more than we do in a third or fortieth work. The Word of God does not teach any. We believe it would be well for all to heed the exhortation in the epistles, and separate themselves more fully unto the Lord and His holy service. We believe there is not a people on the earth that does not need to do this, or scarce an individual. When the people of God will humble themselves and consecrate themselves fully to Him, His power will come upon them in its fulness. Till then there will be a lack.
