Doctor Dixon Answered

In the last few months Dr. A. C. Dixon, pastor of the Moody Church, has preached twice, or more, on the subject of tongues, and recently has published a booklet on the same subject, a copy of which is before me. Feeling that he has not done justice to the subject, and that the public has a right to hear the other side of the question, I make this attempt to answer some of the statements which he makes. I shall have only time to touch on a very few points, and space compels me to deal briefly with those I shall be able to touch on at all. I wish to state that I always had a very high regard for Mr. Dixon, as I have believed him to be faithfully preaching Christ as the Savior, and standing firmly for the Bible as the Word of God. I have no desire to say or do any thing against him, or to in any way injure him. I simply write in defense of what I believe to be the plain truth of God, and to which I believe my brother has failed to do justice.

In the first place Mr. Dixon admits of a doubt as to whether the Apostles and others on the day of Pentecost really spoke in other tongues or whether the people simply heard in their own language. The Scripture says distinctly that they spake in other tongues, and to our mind there is no room whatever for doubting that they really spake in other tongues. On page one, under the head of “Not Repeated” he makes the statement that the Pentecostal experience was never repeated, and continuing attempts to prove that in other instances where the speaking in tongues is recorded, it does not mean that the people spake in other tongues, but if I grasp his meaning, they simply spoke in a different way in the same language. Let us examine the Scriptures and see if Dr. Dixon is right in this position. His position is that the Pentecostal experience was never repeated. In Acts 10:47, Peter says of the people at the house of Cornelius, “They have received the Holy Ghost as well as we.” In Acts 11:15, Peter says, “The Holy Spirit fell on them even as on us at the beginning.” Now as it was the speaking in other tongues, or as Mr. Dixon puts it, tongues, leaving off the adjective, “other” that convinced both Peter and those that were with him, that the gentiles had received the gift of the Holy Ghost, it is an astonishing thing to me that a man of the learning of Dr. Dixon should not see that it was supernatural tongues that were spoken.

We believe that Peter’s plain, twice-repeated statement that these people had received the same thing he received on the day of Pentecost, entirely removes this flimsy foundation from under our brother’s argument. We cannot see that the absence of visible tongues of fire or of the sound of the rushing, mighty wind has anything to do with what they received or with the tongues that followed. It was the Holy Ghost that was received on the day of Pentecost, and it was the Holy Ghost that was received at the house of Cornelius. In each case it was evidenced by the speaking in tongues, as the Spirit gave utterance. Dr. Dixon uses the same weak argument with regard to the Words of our blessed Lord Who said: “These signs shall follow them that believe: in my name they shall cast out demons; they shall speak with new tongues.” To our mind there can be no doubt as to what the Lord meant, nor have we ever heard any question raised as to His meaning till recently. All have been agreed, so far as we know, that He meant supernatural tongues, and in Acts 2 we see how beautifully it was fulfilled. The same thing applies to Acts 19:6.

On page two Mr. Dixon takes up the subject of the speaking in tongues at Corinth as recorded in the 14th chapter of 1 Cor. After admitting what is generally denied by the opposers of the Pentecostal work, namely that there is a difference between the speaking in tongues as the Spirit gives utterance, and the exercising the gift of tongues, as at Corinth, where it is plainly implied that the speaker has control of himself, and can speak or not as he chooses, he takes up the subject of the gift of tongues and the gift of interpretation. To our mind our brother is in the grossest possible error on both these subjects. In answering him on these points I am going to put Scripture and facts against his theories. On page four, paragraph four, he says concerning the gift of tongues “it was an ecstatic rhapsodical experience, which expressed emotion without thought.” Paul says in 1 Cor. 12:4–10, that certain gifts are given in the Spirit, and tongues is classed as one of those gifts. It is a travesty on Scripture to teach that that which it calls a gift of the Holy Spirit, is simply “ecstatic,” “rhapsodical” or emotional. The speaking in tongues is a genuine gift of the Spirit of God, and there is not a hint in Scripture that it is an inferior gift, or that it is not to be sought. Can it be possible that this man of letters really believes that God would bestow a gift of the Spirit on his people that was of as little value as he would lead us to believe the gift of tongues is? Repeatedly he refers to the speaking in tongues, as “ecstatic,” “rhapsodical,” “This gift of ecstatic joy,” and in other ways clearly implies that it has no more meaning than a laugh or a shout, making it emotionalism pure and simple. The Word of God calls it a gift of the Holy Spirit, and says that the speaker speaks to God. Can it be that God would commit to His children a means of communication with Himself, that was as unimportant and insignificant as Dr. Dixon makes the gift of tongues appear to be? Three years ago I heard Dr. Dixon in delivering an address say that the speaking in tongues was simply a spiritual ecstacy language, and was the result of a person’s getting so happy they lost control of themselves, and simply gave vent to their feelings in unintelligible gibberish, and that the gift of interpretation, simply meant that at such a time some one would stand up and explain to the people that the one speaking in tongues was not crazy, but simply so happy that he had lost control of himself. This in substance is repeated in the article which we have under discussion. His whole contention, when analyzed, is that the speaking in tongues is simply ecstatic utterances escaping a person when they are rapturously happy, and that interpretation simply means to explain that this is the case. Would it be necessary for God to give a person a gift of the Holy Spirit to produce the former or to explain it? I appeal this case to the intelligence of every reader of this article.

Our contention is that the speaking in tongues is supernatural. The Scriptures say that in the Spirit mysteries are spoken. We contend that to interpret means to really translate what is spoken. We believe that the mysteries spoken in the Spirit are brought down into the realms of the natural where the understanding of man can grasp them, by the Spirit’s operating the gift of interpretation. The Spirit through one speaks mysteries, and through another interprets them. This view of things exalts these blessed gifts of the Spirit to the place where they belong. Dr. Dixon’s teaching on this subject entirely removes the Scriptural teaching that they are gifts of the Spirit, and makes them to appear very insignificant, as, if what he says were true, anyone who was happy enough might speak in tongues, and a sinner could interpret as well as any one else. Let the reader decide for himself which is right.

Let us compare Dr. Dixon’s statements concerning “these ecstatic utterances” with actual facts. Is it only when those who speak in tongues are rapturously happy that they speak in tongues? The writer has been filled with the Holy Spirit and speaking in tongues for nearly three and one half years, and can say from actual experience that Mr. Dixon’s ideas on this subject are entirely wrong; and with all his learning and wisdom, and knowledge on all other lines, he has no knowledge whatever of this experience. Fifty-thousand copies of this paper will be circulated. They will fall into the hands of thousands of people who are speaking in tongues, all of whom will bear me out in this statement. The first time I ever spoke in tongues was March 2, 1907. The Spirit had come upon me, and I was prostrated under his power. This was the day I was baptized in the Spirit. I was conscious at the time that the personal Holy Spirit had come and taken up His abode within me. He was dealing with me in a wondrous way, when presently He began to operate upon my vocal organs, and then to speak through me in tongues.

There was nothing ecstatic or emotional about it, in the sense of which Dr. Dixon speaks. I was happy and continued to be happy, but it was not my happiness, nor emotions that produced the speaking in tongues. I spoke as the Spirit gave utterance, as the disciples at Pentecost, and it was the operation of the Holy Ghost that caused the speaking in tongues, as well as to make me happy. From that time to this I have spoken in tongues almost every day, and often many times in a day, but I am just as apt to speak when under a burden for the lost, or for the work of the Lord, or when in earnest prayer, as when I am rapturously happy. The Holy Spirit dwelling within speaks when He wills, and I am glad to have it so.

It is the same with interpretation. Time and again has He given me the interpretation of messages spoken in tongues, and at different times when others would stand and give the interpretation of what He had spoken in tongues through me, I would have the same clear interpretation, which is wonderfully strengthening to one’s faith. What a contrast between these actual facts experienced in the lives of thousands of God’s people today, and the theories set forth by my Brother Dixon.

On page 7, paragraph 5, Dr. Dixon makes the astonishing statement that the speaking in tongues was a sign of unbelief rather than of faith. I wonder if any student of the Scriptures will ever believe this? Will anyone believe that it was unbelief in the Apostles on the day of Pentecost that caused them to speak in tongues? Will anyone believe that the speaking in tongues at Ephesus indicated unbelief? Are lovers of the Bible ready to believe that one of the gifts the Holy Spirit imparts to those who receive Him, is a sign that the recipient is an unbeliever, or that he is weak in the faith? Let us appeal the case to Jesus Christ, Who says, “These signs shall follow them that believe.” The speaking in tongues according to the Word of God is a sign of believers, and a sign to unbelievers. If what Dr. Dixon says of it be true it would be a thing to be feared, as no one would want to possess anything that branded him before the world as an unbeliever. Is it not astonishing that the Apostle Paul should say, “I would that ye all spoke in tongues,” when so doing would brand them as unbelievers, and then to make himself still more ridiculous, exclaim, “I thank my God I speak with tongues more than you all,” when so doing, according to Dr. Dixon, would brand him as the greatest unbeliever of all? What will lovers of Bible truth think of such teaching from a man who fills the position this man fills? Knowing that large numbers of people will be unwilling to believe that Mr. Dixon taught such a thing, and will believe that I am trying to injure him by accusing him of doing so, I refer anyone who doubts to “Speaking in Tongues” by A. C. Dixon, address The Bible Institute, 826 La Salle Ave., Chicago.

Dr. Dixon is very firm in his stand that it is a lack of faith to expect any sign to accompany the receiving of the Holy Spirit. He implies that those who expect to speak in tongues when they are baptized in the Holy Spirit are a “wicked and adulterous generation.” But is this true? Does it betray a lack of faith in God and His word to expect Him to do what He says He will? Is it wrong to expect that when we are justified by faith, we will have peace with God? Is it wrong to expect the Spirit Himself to bear witness with our spirits that we are the children of God? Would it be wrong for one claiming to be a Christian and who had not these evidences of salvation, to concern himself about the matter, and pray that God would give him conscious salvation?

Is it possible that things have so changed, that a person who is clearly convinced by the Scriptures that he has not the baptism in the Spirit must be satisfied to see that Jesus promised to send a comforter even though he has no knowledge of ever receiving Him? Could a sinner claim salvation in the same way? Why did not Peter and the rest of the Apostles after Christ ascended to the Father simply say, “Well He promised to send the Comforter, therefore we have Him, and it would be unbelief to go to the upper room and tarry?” Does anyone believe that when Peter and John went down to the city of Samaria, as recorded in the eighth of Acts, they told the converts that they must not expect to receive any thing, but must believe they had the Holy Spirit, and that was all there was to it? Would Simon, the sorcerer, have been so impressed by such proceedings that he would have offered Peter money to give him power to go through such a form? The truth of the matter is this. When people receive the Holy Ghost, there are signs which follow, without anyone’s seeking for them, and they are following in thousands of cases today. This is so troubling those who have none of the Scriptural signs of the baptism in the Holy Spirit, that they seem determined at any cost to minimize the work the Lord is doing, or discredit it altogether. The Apostles prayed that signs and wonders might be wrought in the name of the Holy Child Jesus, and I do not think they made any mistake in so doing. Paul says, “Covet earnestly the best gifts,” and again, “Desire spiritual gifts,” and to our mind he was not in error. Every thing that comes from God is a gift. Our advice to every sinner would be to seek till he finds God’s gift to him, that is, Jesus Christ the only Saviour. And to everyone who has received Him, we would say, seek to receive what He has to give you, namely the gift of the Holy Spirit. To those who have received the Holy Spirit, we would say keep low at the feet of Jesus and ask Him to give you the gifts of the Spirit, that Jesus Christ may be glorified through you in any way He chooses. Space forbids my dealing with other points which I should like to answer, so I prayerfully submit this article to the judgment of its readers, who I trust will examine the Scriptures to see if these things be so.

I submit the following proposition to Dr. Dixon: I will engage a large hall in the central part of the city, and pay all the expenses on it, if he will agree to meet me in a friendly discussion of this much discussed subject before the people. I will guarantee that there will be not less than 500 Pentecostal people present at this meeting. I believe there would be a thousand, but will guarantee five hundred. This will afford our brother an excellent opportunity to present his side of the subject to the Pentecostal people, and I am glad to have them hear him. This discussion, if Dr. Dixon agrees, is to be a friendly one, affording each one of us an opportunity to present his side of the question, and as this subject is being so widely discussed in the religious world today, we believe it would not only be of interest to the public, but profitable as well. All Mr. Dixon will have to do will be to appear, and deliver his address. All arrangements will be made for the meeting and all expenses paid.

We can see no grounds our brother can have for rejecting this proposition, unless he should feel that it would be unbending too much from his dignity. We should hope, however, that as this work is growing and spreading so rapidly, and as he has taken up arms against it, giving it as much attention as he has, he will be willing to take one more step, and give the public a chance to hear the two sides presented at the same time.

I have ordered fifty thousand copies of this paper, and if Mr. Dixon rejects this proposition, the hundreds of thousands of readers, which will include preachers and missionaries of this and many other lands, can decide why he did so. Finally, will every reader of this paper earnestly pray for the pastor of the Moody Church, that God will have His way with him? And please pray for the writer of this article, who is the least of all the servants of the Lord.

The Great Revival at Azusa Street Mission: How It Began and How It Ended

On February 14th, we began meetings in Azusa Mission. From the first day the power of God rested upon the meetings in a wonderful way. The altar was crowded at every service, and after the first few meetings, it was necessary to provide extra altar space, and soon we moved the seekers’ meetings to the second floor, where there is a large room fitted up for that purpose. The work in Los Angeles was in a sad condition. Those who had been the leaders, in most cases, had proven so incompetent that the saints had lost all confidence in them, and this had resulted in a state of confusion that was sad indeed to see. Scores were really in a backslidden state, and yet in their hearts they longed to follow Jesus. Scores of others were, and for months had been, crying to God to send some one who would preach the truth and lead His people on. The suffering of many had been great indeed. As the message began to go forth, the saints came from all directions, and inside of a few days the place was crowded to the doors, and many turned away. Sometimes there would be more than a hundred at the altar at a single service. One after another would stand up in the meetings and confess that they had gotten their eyes off Jesus, and go to the altar, and in almost every case the anointing of the blessed Spirit would be renewed, till soon the very air was filled with notes of praise and shouts of victory.

From the very first, sinners were saved, and an average of at least ten a week were baptized in the Holy Spirit and spoke in tongues, as He gave them utterance. Week after week went by, and still the interest did not wane, but on the contrary the power increased, till the glory of God literally filled the place. At times the Spirit would move upon the saints, and they would sing in the Spirit, and praise the Lord in the most wonderful way I ever heard. At times there could be no regular order of service; no one could preach or even testify. All we could do was to sit with our souls bathed in a sea of heavenly glory, and praise the Lord with all our hearts.

As stated above, the sufferings of many of the saints had been great. Their joy now knew no bounds. They saw in these wonderful meetings the direct answer to the earnest prayers they had sent up to God for months, and now they knew their labor had not been in vain, and the light of Heaven began to shine from their faces in a way most marvelous to behold. God had told some of them He was going to do a work in Azusa St. Mission, and they now rejoiced in the fulfillment of His promise. Some saw visions of the cloud of glory hanging over the place, and had revelations of what God was going to do, every one of which came true. Time and space forbid our giving anything like a detailed account of the meetings. As many as twenty-two were baptized in the Holy Spirit in one week. Some of the hardest sinners were saved. I believe that literally hundreds who had more or less backslidden were restored, and many real cases of healing were witnessed.

When we arrived in this city, we tried hard to be in fellowship with the Upper Room Mission, of which Mr. Fisher was then Pastor, but we were denied the privilege of speaking there, and refused fellowship, on the grounds that we were crooked in doctrine, in that we did not believe that sanctification was a definite, second work of grace. So when the meetings began Mr. Fisher, with many others who believe the second work of grace theory, seemed to feel it their duty to do all in their power against us. As a result, we were condemned and denounced in the most bitter terms. The people were warned against us, and told that those who were getting the baptism under our ministry were getting false baptisms. This was not confined to Los Angeles, but all up and down this Coast, my teaching has been denounced as from the pit, and all sorts of charges have been made against me. In a word, the most bitter persecution and opposition has raged against me from the day God began to work so marvelously in Azusa St.

Some one will ask what doctrine I preach that has brought all this upon me. In answer I will say that I preach the finished work of Calvary, that we come into Christ and are fully saved in conversion, and that the next step is to be baptized in water, and then in the Holy Spirit; that we do not, according to the Scriptures, have to seek for any intermediate experience. We exhort to stand on the Word of God rather than any experience, to hold on to Christ rather than to something He has given us, to abide in Him, and not in some experience. We believe that in conversion we come into Christ, and are saved and sanctified, and that we are to reckon ourselves dead, and in living faith abide in Christ, and live and walk in the Spirit.

This doctrine commended itself to the saints. The power of God fell, as it was preached. In one case after another God demonstrated His truth by saving and filling people with the Spirit in the same meeting; thus proving His power to work today, as He did in the days of the Apostles, as recorded all through the book of Acts.

Soon the people from the Upper Room Mission began to attend the services, and almost everyone who did so was at once convinced that the mighty power of God was there. Brother George B. Studd, who was associated with Mr. Fisher in the work, came, and was convinced that God was working. He had long been a seeker and had suffered much for the sake of the truth. God showed me that He wanted me to be in fellowship with Brother Studd and that He wanted to baptize him in the Holy Spirit in our meetings, and later that He wanted to separate him from the Upper Room and from Mr. Fisher. True to what He showed me, God baptized him in our meeting, and a little later separated him from Mr. Fisher, and he has been with us ever since, rejoicing and praising God. Meantime Sister Fisher came to our meetings and was baptized in the Holy Spirit, and wonderfully blessed of God. Then came the janitor, the usher and some of the elders and preachers from the Upper Room, and received the baptism. Mr. Fisher came up to the light, and at one time acknowledged it, then turned away, and hardened his heart and opposed the work more bitterly than ever, and today, if I am rightly informed, he is out of the ministry altogether. It is an awful thing to resist the power of God. Those who do so, do it at their own peril. Will the readers of this article please pray for this dear man, that the Lord will restore him?

As the meetings went on, the people on all sides began to ask what Brother Seymour would probably do, when he returned from the East. He had begun to write and wire for money to come home on. Some said he would oppose the work, others said he would accept it. The Spirit put a great burden upon my soul, and showed me clearly that he was trying to get home to get possession of the work, and that if he could not do so, he would do all in his power to stop it. I told this to several people before he arrived, and after he arrived, before he had taken his stand. Meantime Brother Seymour came, and instead of making the honest confession he owed the people, for the way he had compromised and denied the truth, and then taking a humble place, till such time as he had regained the confidence of the people, he attempted to push himself on the people, and preach to them against their will, and a little later, notified me that this was his work, and that he wanted his place. I tried to reason with him, telling him that it would ruin the work to place him in charge at that time, but he showed a very bitter spirit and condemned and judged the people, saying that if the people did not want to hear him they could leave. When he said this I knew that it was useless to try to reason with him further. I saw plainly that God had shown me the truth concerning him. He does not care in the least for the work of the Lord, but wants a place in it. If he can not have the place, he will not hesitate to tear down the work.

The next day I asked for an expression from the congregation, as to whether they wanted him to take charge of the work, or me to continue. With the exception of ten, or less, the congregation, consisting of several hundred people, voted that the meetings should continue, as they were. The glory and power of God continued to rest mightily upon the meetings, and that day several were baptized in the Holy Spirit. This was Sunday.

When we came to the Mission Tuesday we found that Seymour had influenced a few of the officers of the Mission, men of his own color, to stand with him, and they had locked and bolted the door. It developed that for days, while we were preaching, praying and seeking God in the Mission, Seymour had been scheming and planning as to how he could get possession of the building, if he could not get the work. This last move was necessary to let all men see what manner of man he has come to be. Many of us who knew him when the power and glory of God was so mightily upon him years ago, could never have turned away and left him with God, if he had not done something that would convince us beyond a doubt that he had gotten into such a condition that the power of God had entirely left him, and that he was no longer worthy of the confidence and respect of the saints. I have been the last of all the brethren, that I know of, to give him up, and have always found an excuse for his failures and blunders; but now I am compelled to acknowledge that the brethren have been right, and that, though once a mighty man, he is such no longer. Sadly do I pen these lines, and I hope every reader will pray that the Lord will restore him.

We all saw in this move a tremendous effort on the part of Satan to force us into a compromise. Failing in this, he succeeded in having us turned out of the place that was paid for with consecrated money for a place of worship. Thus we were turned into the street in the very midst of one of the greatest revivals we ever saw. It took us some little time to see that this was really God’s way of separating us from an element who were not loyal to Him, and into a larger and better place as well. For a day or two there was a little confusion, as many could not understand what had happened. Then God led us to a large, airy hall at the corner of Seventh and Los Angeles streets which we could lease for a year, and we did so. By the help of the Lord we had it ready for the Sunday services, and from the first meeting the power and glory of God has been mightily upon us. In another article I will give an account of the present condition of the work in Los Angeles, as space forbids in this article.

With joy I have told of the beginning of the great revival at dear old Azusa St. Mission, and with real grief I have told of how it ended, and why. Let none of the saints condemn me, or think I have desired to condemn Mr. Seymour or Mr. Fisher or anyone else. The circumstances have forced this most unpleasant duty upon me. The news of the outpouring at Azusa brought rejoicing wherever it went; and so many letters of inquiry have reached me, that I feel it my duty to tell the saints everywhere just what happened, and who is responsible for it.

Concerning Self-Defense, Misrepresentations, etc.

In the last year several tracts and several articles in religious papers, as well as numerous false reports have been circulated against us. The only reason that we know for this, is that we stand for the Finished Work of Calvary, instead of the old theory of two works of grace, and that some are jealous of the little success the Lord has given us. We are ready to believe that some who have written or reported, that we did not believe in sanctification, did so from their own mistaken idea, that only those who are sanctified as a second work of grace are sanctified at all. There is little excuse for them, however, as we have declared in all our sermons and written articles, when we referred to the subject at all, that we never believed stronger in entire sanctification, and that we believe that it is the single standard of the New Testament. “Without Holiness no man shall see the Lord,” has been our battle cry. We are also willing to believe, that we have been somewhat misrepresented by those who had not a clear understanding of our real position and teaching. We fully believe, however, that most of the false reports circulated against us have been willful and malicious. It is a real grief to us to make this statement, but we know that actual facts warrant our doing so.

Some of the reports circulated against us have created a real prejudice against us. This cuts off our opportunity for doing good to those thus prejudiced. In different places saints have come to us, after hearing us preach a few times, and said, “Is this really William H. Durham?” When assured that it was, they have declared that they were greatly surprised, as they had heard such awful reports about what I preached and believed, and the spirit I did it in. In one case after another, such persons have sent for their friends and gotten them to the meetings, and in some cases they would get the baptism. In such cases, they often say, “How could they ever circulate such things against you?” The only answer that I know to give is that their attitude seems to be, “Why should we not circulate anything against him that will injure his reputation, he does not believe in two works of grace, and we do?”

Our desire has always been to keep still, and never speak a word in our own defense. God has long ago brought us to the place that it does not hurt us, in the least, to be falsely accused and condemned. At times, however, the attitude of most enemies, and some friends, has been, “Why does he not defend himself, if he is innocent?” There has never been one time that we were not perfectly capable of doing so, and at the same time exposing those who have written and spoken falsely against us. We have been publishing editions of fifty thousand copies of this paper; it contains sixteen pages and we are handy with the pen. The reason we have not answered our critics, or rather the reasons why we are not conducting that sort of a campaign, are: first, because we do not believe the Lord and our thousands of friends in this and other countries want us to take up the time defending ourselves; second, we are determined to reserve the space in this paper for the printing of the real Gospel of the Son of God. If we began to fill our space with answers to opposers, we would woefully misrepresent the Pentecostal movement. We know of one mission of some strength on the Pacific Coast that stands for the second work of grace. From there to the Atlantic Coast, I do not know of one mission of any strength that stands for two works. From one ocean to the other every mission, that I know of, is open to me. I have urgent calls to come, at the first opportunity, and preach the Finished Work of Calvary in most of them. I am not going to recognize that there is a faction of any importance that still stands for the second work. Further, in cases where I could do so, I have no desire to publish before the world the failures or downfall of my enemies. If I am right, God will be with me. If they are wrong, they will only go so far, and the Lord will call a halt. I can say with sadness, that it has seemed that I did not need to do anything to pull most of them down.

In different cases I have letters and documents, signed by those who have done the most underhanded and unChristian acts against me; which prove conclusively that all they have done was done in malice and hypocrisy. In all these cases I have had perfect knowledge of this all the time. Some of them have come to me in bitterness of soul and confessed their sin. Some have said they were largely influenced and led to do what they did by others. Others have said they could not possibly understand whatever moved them to do such a thing. During all these things, my attitude has been one of silence. I can trust the Lord to work things out. When you see that people have little or no regard for either truth, or righteousness, it is always best to leave them with the Lord.

A little paper published at Cleveland, Tenn., lately contains the latest, most absurd, and absolutely false report of an imaginary happening in one of my meetings, that we ever heard. Only envy and malice could have prompted it. In it I was accused of ejecting a person from a meeting for testifying to two works of grace. No one was ever in any place denied the privilege by me of testifying to as many works of grace as they desired. With grief, I will say that our ministers and the saints in considerable number have not only been put out, after testifying to the Finished Work, but have been waited on before the service began, and told that they could not speak, sing or pray in the meeting. In one case after another, our people have been shamefully insulted, rebuked and denounced; but in not one case have we ever disfellowshipped any person, because he believed in two works of grace. I have always told our people that, no difference how many works of grace anyone believed in, if he did not show the spirit of Christ, he was not of Him. I have repeatedly warned the people never to show the spirit that has been shown against them.

Finally, brethren, our plan in the future shall be as it has been in the past. We shall make no attempt to answer false and foolish reports circulated against us. We shall clearly set forth from time to time our full belief in the pages of this paper. If you think we ought to speak in our own defense, remember it would consume too much time. If you think we should not refer to these things, even as in this article, remember that a statement is sometimes necessary. In all cases, grant us the benefit of your prayers and the privilege of devoting our entire time and strength to preaching and publishing this blessed Gospel of the Son of God. We have no personal matter, and no personal complaint.

A Word to Ministers, from a Minister

There is a deep-felt need among ministers everywhere, today, that can only be met by their receiving the gift of the Holy Ghost. There is nothing that can ever take His place in the life of a preacher of the Gospel of Jesus Christ. No one can have the inward revelation of Jesus Christ which is necessary to successfully preach Him, as the only savior of men, till it is given him by the blessed Holy Spirit. No one can know the value of the Blood of Jesus Christ, in the fullest sense, till it is revealed to him by the Spirit of God. In fact, it is very doubtful if the Scriptures authorize anyone to preach, till he is filled with the Holy Spirit.

After the Lord Jesus Christ arose from the dead, He commanded His disciples to tarry at Jerusalem, till they were endued with power from on high (Luke 24:49). In Acts 1:4 He forbids their leaving the city, till the Holy Spirit should fall on them. By this, we see that it was the purpose of our Lord, that His ministers should be filled with the Spirit, and that theirs should be a ministry of power through the Spirit. We can find no place in the Scriptures where this order of things was ever changed, and it is sickening to read articles today, some of them by learned divines, declaring that God has changed His plans, and that we are living in an age when God is perfectly [illegible]; and that any miraculous works that are done today, are done by Satan and his agents. Such teaching is a travesty on Scripture, a slur on the Holy Ghost, and an insult to God, as well as an awful accusation against hundreds of thousands of the purest saints on earth today. It is gratifying to know that the class of ministers last mentioned are few in number, and we dare to hope that their tribe will soon become extinct, and that they will be replaced by men called of God, equipped by the Lord, filled with the Holy Ghost, who will fearlessly preach Christ and His blessed Gospel, instead of trying to explain it away, as these men are doing. On the other hand it seems that the coming of the Lord is the only relief for the situation, as unbelief and higher criticism are getting such a strong hold on many, that we fear their power will never be broken.

Men have made the mistake everywhere of trying to prepare themselves for the ministry. Only God can prepare a man to preach Christ. God’s way of preparing a man is, first to soundly convert him, and second, to fill him with the Holy Ghost, and then give him a definite call. God will also give him a real longing for the salvation of the lost, and he will preach to save men, and to please God. Such a minister will not be self-conscious; he will be God-conscious. He will not seek his own; he will seek the good of humanity, and the glory of God. He will tell all the truth, no matter how many enemies it makes him, and while he will grieve to see those who do not want the truth turn away from him, he will rejoice that he has grace to obey and strive to please God. He will never preach to please men, and make friends, or to get their support. He will preach to men under conviction for sin, and then patiently lead them to the Christ who pardons and saves, and then tell them, they still need the Holy Ghost. A God-equipped, and called minister will never compromise with anybody.

Ministers who prepare themselves, or are prepared by man, will have a need in their own lives, and in spite of themselves, will be conscious of it all the time. This will result in weaknesses, which will be felt by them, and seen by others. They will not have any real burden for the salvation of the lost, in this and other lands. They will have a desire to please men, and to win their approval and support. Their ministry will be a profession instead of a calling. They will depend on their salary, instead of trusting God for all things. They will often compromise the truth, or withhold it in part at least, because they desire to win the applause and support of men, rather than to please and glorify God.

Men are spending years in seminaries, universities, and colleges, preparing for the ministry, and in their eagerness to acquire intellectual knowledge, their spiritual life is many times sadly neglected. Many come out of these institutions, through which they have expected so much help, in a much worse condition spiritually, than when they enter them. Many of these institutions are honey-combed with higher criticism, and instead of the young man’s faith in God and His Word being strengthened, as he expected it would be, it is sadly weakened. Many have told us of the damaging effect the teaching they have received at these institutions has had upon them. Some have said that these things have proven the hardest obstacles they have had to surmount when they really sought to know God, as they felt it was their duty as ministers to know Him. We have dealt with ministers, who, after finishing their regular courses here, have gone abroad, both for travel and study, and who have since spent years in the ministry, and who tell us of the disappointment of it all, so far as the satisfying of their souls is concerned. They tell us of years of real heart hunger, and thirst, which nothing seemed to satisfy. So far as our knowledge extends, this same thirst exists in the souls of most ministers today.

To our mind these things go a long way toward proving, that men are seeking in the wrong direction for preparation for the work of the ministry. We believe that as good as education is, it falls far short of meeting the need of the day, and that we will have to look in an entirely different direction, if the need is to be met. We wish to say to every brother minister everywhere, that God has made full provision for the need. The need is the Holy Ghost. Nothing can ever take His place in the life of any believer, and especially that of a minister. The learned and eloquent need Him as much as others. It is not the work of ministers to charm people by their eloquence, but to preach men under such conviction, that they will turn to God. The world has had so much of the wisdom of man and so little of the power of God, that it seems to us, it is high time for us as ministers of Christ, to go down before the Lord in true humility of heart, and tarry, till He really endues us with power from on high.

Some will say, “The Lord will not fill us now as at Pentecost, and in Bible days,” but to such we answer, that the proof that God will do it is that He is doing it in thousands of cases and in every part of the earth, and what God does for one of His ministers or children, He will do for anyone of them, if they will meet His conditions.

As is always the case when men seek in the wrong direction for a thing, more labor and pains is required, and in the end they fall short of receiving it. They go from one thing to another, until we are reminded of the wanderings of Israel in the wilderness. One thing after another is investigated, until many give up in despair, or become infidels, or higher critics, which amounts to about the same thing. We are reminded of the ship whose crew were perishing for water, and when their signal of distress was answered by another vessel, which inquired what the distress was, and having learned, said to them, “Let down your buckets, you are in the mouth of the Amazon!” They were perishing for water when there were millions of tons of it flowing right under their vessel.

To every minister of the Gospel, we would say, “There is an open fountain.” If you have tried many things and failed to receive what your soul craves, get down and cry to God, till He comes and meets your soul, and satisfies you. If you have spent years in study, and travel, and still feel a deep need in your own heart, cease to expect from any source except God. Read the Acts of the Apostles. Note well the experiences given there. Tell God you will never rest, till He has given you what they received. Humble your heart before Him. Set up an altar just where you are, and begin to pray and wait; claim His promise and honestly expect that He will meet you, and He will do so.

Satan will tell you that this is too much for you to expect, and that you can never receive. Where in the Scriptures are we authorized to go on preaching the Gospel with anything less than what we are asking you to seek, and expect to receive? The writer speaks from actual experience, as he preached for more than five years, with a conscious shortage in his own experience, but when God sent him the light, he received it, and became a seeker, and the Lord met him, and filled him with the Holy Spirit, with the sign of tongues as evidence that it was the Bible brand. This experience has stood the test for two years and three months, and even as he writes these lines, his whole being is glowing with the power of the living God. Facts cannot be gainsaid. We are speaking from our hearts, and from tested knowledge of the experience itself. We are sending out this paper at a great sacrifice, of labor and money, and all the reward we expect is the good which we earnestly hope, and dare to believe, it will do.

Again, there is a great hungering and thirsting among the people, and it seems they are waiting for the ministers to be filled with the Holy Spirit, and lead them into the things of God. Brethren, our opportunity is now. Let us grasp it. All any minister has to do in these days is to tarry till the Holy Spirit falls on him, and the revival starts. There is a revival spirit among the people; and there is a great need of ministers who will take the Bible and fearlessly preach it. How sad it is to us to see so many ministers holding back, and waiting to see what the people are going to say about this movement. Others are taking what those they look upon as leaders say about the work. Brethren, these men have not investigated this work. They have not told the truth about it. Their criticisms have reached me by scores. Not one of them has been fair, or true to the facts in the case. None of them has done what they could have done to inform themselves on the subject. Many of those who are looked upon as leaders live in Chicago, and know our address, and could learn the truth by attending one Sunday morning service, and two or three consecutive services during the week. They have not done so, but have made grave and utterly false charges against the movement; such as that we start people to seeking for tongues, and that we are not interested in the salvation of sinners, etc., which, of course, is utterly false. Satan is hoisting scarecrows in every direction to keep the people away.

Brother, do you dare to read the first ten chapters of the Acts, and then ask God to give you exactly what He gave the Apostles on the day of Pentecost, and what He gave the converts at the city of Samaria, and the believers at the house of Cornelius, and then wait for Him to do it? Do not ask Him for tongues; ask Him to give you the gift of the Holy Ghost. Ask Him to baptize you without your speaking in tongues, if He ever baptizes people that way, and you will find that when His mighty power falls upon you that you will speak in tongues, as all the rest of us have done. You ask what is the good of the tongues? They are the evidence that what you receive is the Bible brand. It is a Pentecostal baptism we are talking about.

A German Methodist preacher who was baptized in the Holy Ghost here last week, prayed that the Lord would not let him speak in tongues unless that always followed; but when the Spirit fell on him he spoke in tongues clearly for half an hour. Pastor Bell, whose testimony appears in this number, prayed the same way, and with the same results. We will say here what we have preached, and contended for for two years, that we would not give five cents to have everybody in the city of Chicago speak in tongues, unless it was the direct result of their being filled with the Holy Ghost, as the disciples were on the day of Pentecost. This will convince any honest soul, that we are not trying to get people to receive the gift of tongues.

Let us search the Scriptures, and see if these things are so. The Church of Pentecost was made up of men who possessed little learning; but there is not a church on earth today, that has the power in it, that they had. They had the power of the Holy Ghost. They had the power of the Name of Jesus Christ. They knew the value of His Blood. When men stood in their presence they were pricked in their hearts. It was not their learning or eloquence that convicted and convinced men, it was the power of the Holy Ghost, and that is what is needed today. There is an awful falling away from God and His truth in these days, and in our humble judgment, it is very largely due to the fact that the ministry is not filled with the Spirit of God. If all ministers were filled with the Holy Spirit, and preaching Christ as it is the duty of ministers to do, such things as Christian Science, and spiritualism, could not exist. Satan knows there is a real hunger in the hearts of God’s people for the Comforter which Jesus promised, and that Christians know there should be power in their lives; and while the church of God is asleep, he is cunning and crafty enough to palm off his counterfeits on souls who do not know the truth. To my mind, we, as ministers, are largely responsible for the present condition of things; and the Lord will hold us accountable, if we do not humble ourselves before the Lord, and the people, and seek till we are filled with the Holy Spirit, and give the people the real bread of life. They will then receive the gift of the Holy Spirit, and find all their hearts desire in Jesus Christ and His blessed Truth.

Finally, while God recognizes only a ministry that is in the Holy Spirit, He has provided a way whereby every one of His ministers can have all their needs supplied, and that by simply believing, and obeying Him, and asking for the Holy Spirit, and waiting till He comes upon them. We then can say, with Paul, “My preaching was not in the wisdom of men, but in the demonstration of the Spirit and of power.” And again, “I was determined not to know anything among you, save Jesus Christ and Him crucified.” How few can say this! Brethren, what right have we to preach a Bible in which we believe very little? What right have we to preach a Christ on whom we believe so little? How dare we preach unless we fully believe?

I prayerfully submit this article for the consideration of ministers everywhere, and will be glad to pray for any who desire it, and even though they do not send request, we will pray for the thousands to whom we mail copies of this paper, knowing that we shall meet everyone of them at the judgment bar of God, where we shall all give an account to Him who has called us to the ministry of the Gospel of His Son. Brethren, pray for me.

The Church

We are frequently asked to give our opinion concerning the Church, as to what it is, of whom composed, etc. We are also asked, frequently, whether in our opinion Pentecostal people should stay in and support the churches in this day. We have seldom answered such questions, as it seems to us every one should understand these things as soon as they were spiritually enlightened and had their understanding opened, so that they would understand the Scriptures. In the first place, the Church of Jesus Christ is composed of Pentecostal people. There never was a Church until after Pentecost, and there is none recognized in the New Testament Scriptures, except the Body of Christ, of which He is the Head, and which is set in order by the Holy Spirit: for the Scriptures declare, 1 Cor. 12:18, “But now hath God set the members, every one of them, in the body as it hath pleased Him.” Now, as it is declared in Ephesians 1:22 that Christ is the Head of the Church, and, in the Scripture quoted above, that God sets the Church in order, and each one is set in the place that the gifts of the Spirit they have received qualifies them to fill, it is clear that only those who are members of Christ’s Body—“For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body,” 1 Cor. 12:13—and set in order by the Holy Spirit, are recognized as being members of the New Testament Church. We have an abnormal Christianity in the world today (that is, those we must recognize as Christians, but who are not filled with the Holy Spirit) for which it is impossible to find any Scriptural provision. In other words, only Spirit-filled people are recognized as being in a place that they are pleasing to God. Wherever we find converts in the New Testament who are not filled with the Holy Spirit, we find the Apostles dealing with them to lead them into the experience.

We conclude, therefore, that a Church, from a Scriptural standpoint, is a company of people who are called out of the world, made new creatures in Christ Jesus, buried with Him by baptism into death, and filled with the Holy Spirit. From such a company the Holy Spirit selects those whom He knows to be qualified for the ministry, and gives them a definite call to preach the Gospel. These ministers will have a burning Gospel message filling their hearts and pouring from their lips, and a real burden for the work of the Lord, and soul travail for the lost, and for those who are not up to their privilege in the Gospel. Nothing will ever turn such a minister aside nor cause him to compromise the truth. The wealth of the world would not buy him off, nor can men ever get him under their control or hinder his message from going forth.

The Church of the Scriptures has a real scriptural experience, and holds to and contends for all the truth of the glorious Gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ. She walks before Him in the beauty of holiness in the light of His truth and in the power of His Spirit, and is thus kept entirely separated from the world and sin and the snares of the devil.

The denominational churches of today are of purely human origin. Not one of them has any Scriptural authority for its existence. In other words, God never authorized any man, or set of men, to build and operate a church, nor to receive members into the churches. As said above, people become members of Christ’s true, holy, spiritual Church when they are born of the Spirit and filled with the Spirit, as this is the only normal Scriptural experience; and they are set in order by the blessed Holy Spirit, and equipped for work by the gifts He imparts to them. The churches of men reject very much of the deepest and most precious truth of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, and exclude members and ministers from their fellowship, if they witness that God has done for them the things He promises to do in His Word, and dare to preach the real truth of God.

When a man or church rejects or opposes the vital truths of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, he, or it, becomes the enemy of God and of the Gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ, and a hindrance to souls who are seeking God’s best. The churches of today unanimously reject the glorious Pentecostal outpouring of the Holy Ghost that has brought such untold blessing to tens of thousands of God’s honest children. They also reject the doctrine of divine healing that has brought bodily health to thousands of God’s real saints. Many of them reject the precious Bible doctrine of holiness of heart and life, and some even reject the work of redemption through the Blood of Jesus Christ; making His Blood of no avail. Thus, in a very full sense, they become the enemies of the Cross of Jesus Christ, and are unworthy the respect of all those who love the Gospel of Christ. While posing as the Church of God, they are in reality mere social clubs. Many of their ministers are unregenerate, knowing nothing of the saving grace of our Lord Jesus Christ.

After careful consideration and a wide observation, I am of the honest opinion that, while there are many good people still in the denominations, as institutions they are the greatest hindrance to the advancement of the real cause of Jesus Christ. Further, I believe they are doing more to hinder the people of earth from receiving God’s glorious message of full salvation and the baptism in the Holy Ghost than all other forces combined. I further believe that the ministers are doing much more to hinder than the members are doing. Take the ministers out of the way and give the people the privilege of hearing the Gospel, and it is my opinion that tens of thousands would readily accept it. When they heard the real standard of the Gospel lifted up and Christ exalted as the only Savior of men, and the precious Blood as the only remedy for sin, and the Holy Ghost honored as Comforter, Teacher and Revealer of God’s glorious truth, tens of thousands would fall at the feet of Jesus Christ and surrender their lives to Him. When we take this view of the matter, there can be no question as to the duty of the people of God. God wants the world to have His message, and every loyal child of God wants to co-operate with God in getting His message to the world as quickly as possible. How, then, can God’s children stay in these institutions of men who fight God and hinder the progress of the Gospel, and which are so organized that they never can accept the truth of God? How can God’s children pay their money into these institutions, when it is used to fight God with, and when God’s real Gospel messengers are denied the privilege of preaching the Gospel inside their doors?

In answer to the question which has been asked me from so many sources, I would say, if God has filled you with the Holy Ghost, bear faithful witness to what He has done for you, and to what He wants to do for all His people, and faithfully witness against the sins of your church, and if they receive the message and turn to God, well and good—if not, walk out from them. Some say there is no Pentecostal or Full Gospel work in their locality, and they do not know where to go, yet they say the church in their locality is bitterly opposed to the truth they love so much: some say they feel that they ought to support a work somewhere, and there is no Full Gospel work in their locality. This does not excuse you, dear child of God, for paying your consecrated money into the hands of those who use it to fight the truth of God. You had a thousand times better select missions and works that are preaching and publishing the truth of God, and send your offerings to help carry on the work, or to send it for the support of foreign missions, than to place it in the hands of those who oppose and hinder the truth. If God’s true people would obey the plain command of His Word concerning those who have a form of godliness but deny the power thereof, and turn away from them, the lines would be drawn, and it would soon be apparent to all that they are not the real Church of God. Thus they would lose their influence in the world. Let us search the Word and obey its teachings, receive its experiences, rejoice in its truth, and honor our Blessed God and His Son, Jesus Christ.

An Open Letter to My Brother Ministers in and out of the Pentecostal Movement: A Strong Appeal

We are living in a wonderful day. God is moving very rapidly indeed. The revelation of one precious truth follows another so closely that only those who are in very close touch with the Lord seem able to grasp these precious truths as fast as they are revealed. The result is that many honest souls oppose the truth of God for a time, and then have to humbly acknowledge their mistake, and take their stand with the truth they have opposed. When the great outpouring of the Spirit came to the Pacific Coast five years ago, many were prepared to receive it as from God, and take their stand from the beginning on the side of God and His wonderful work. Others took a firm stand against it and opposed with all their might, only to find themselves arrayed against God, and were compelled to sorrowfully retrace their steps, before they could get in line for the blessing of God upon their souls. Some failed to do this, and today they are entirely destitute of power. They have even lost what power and blessing they once enjoyed. It is sad indeed to see the lifeless, powerless condition many are in, as a result of having opposed the power of God. It is still sadder when we have to acknowledge that many of these cases are ministers who once led God’s people on to victory, but when advanced light and truth came they rejected it, and the people went in ahead of them. In fact, in all ages the preachers seem to be the last to receive the truth of God when it comes. They seem to become so thoroughly established in their theories that the truth makes no impression upon them.

Still another class seemed to see that this wonderful work was of God, but thought it not best to advocate it very strongly, for fear of causing division among the people. They seemed to be afraid to trust the people with the truth. They also excused themselves on the ground that the plain truth reflected so on the experience of so many dear saints, who had lived in the past, that they hardly thought best to proclaim it, or that if preached at all it should be preached very cautiously and apologetically; and many seemed to think it best to abridge or modify it. This class has seemed to feel all the time that they were called to champion the cause of those who have stood against the movement, or those who have lived in the past, and have proven a much greater hindrance in the work than the out-and-out opposers. While God’s faithful ministers have been thundering forth His present-day message in such a fearless, uncompromising way that thousands have been brought face to face with their need, and thus led to seek and find God, these compromisers have gone about soothing the consciences of the really convicted, telling them they could have the Holy Ghost and not speak in tongues, or that they already had the baptism and all they needed to do was to wait for the evidence of tongues, and that it would come in the Lord’s time. All this has been a great hindrance to those who were trying to get the message of God through, and make men feel their responsibility in the matter of accepting or rejecting it. Of course, if the tongues are the evidence, and men reject that part of the message, they are rejecting that much of the message of God. If they are not the evidence, then those who reject this teaching are only rejecting error, and are not only clear, but are to be commended for so doing. Many of us know that the tongues are the evidence of the baptism in the Holy Ghost; and that the Pentecostal message is direct from God, and we can do nothing less than to proclaim it with all our hearts, no matter how much persecution and suffering it may bring upon us. And it has been the grief of our lives for years, to see men who ought to be preaching this blessed message, and standing with us in the front ranks, lagging behind afraid to take a stand.

Some say they see the truth of the Pentecostal message, but do not think it is time to preach it. In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, what possible excuse can there be for withholding a truth from the people when God reveals it? It seems to us that this is a cowardly excuse for compromising the precious truth of God, and withholding it from the people. Brethren, take a stand.

At the present time, we are confronted with a matter which is of just as much importance in the Pentecostal Movement as those referred to above. The people who make up this movement have largely come into it from other churches and holiness movements, and, as in all such cases in the past, have brought much of the teaching of the churches and movements, from whence they came, with them. They have accepted this blessed truth, and it is now necessary to discard error. It somehow seems harder for many to do this than it was for them to accept the truth. The Holy Ghost not only reveals truth, but exposes error as well. When He reveals truth we must accept it, or we will lose out. When He exposes error we must drop it, or we will go into darkness and confusion. God is undertaking to restore His precious truth to His people, and to free them from error as well. His full power can only be demonstrated among a clean, honest people, who accept and prize all His truth, and detest and reject all error. Now it is a small matter for people to give up what has been known as gross error, but when it comes to giving up theories that we have believed to be precious truth for years, it is another thing, but in these days we are called upon in many cases to do that very thing. Especially is this true with regard to the theory that sanctification is a second, definite work of grace.

Four years and four months ago God baptized me in the Holy Ghost, and from that day to this, I could never preach a sermon on the second work of grace theory. I had held to it for years, and continued to do so for some time, but could not preach on the subject again. I could preach Christ, and could preach holiness as never before, but not as a second work of grace.

Soon the Spirit began to reveal in my heart the finished work of Christ on the Cross of Calvary, but it was so contrary to all that I had taught, and been taught, that I dared not admit, even to myself, that I could find nothing in the Word of God to establish the doctrine that sanctification was a definite second work of grace. Still the Spirit kept revealing in my heart the precious Gospel as preached by the Apostles: identification with Jesus Christ in His death, burial and resurrection. This led me to pray and search the Word of God as never before, and the more I searched, the plainer it was to me that many Pentecostal preachers, myself included, were preaching a doctrine that God’s Word did not teach. After a long and careful examination of the Scriptures and much earnest prayer, I began to preach this blessed and simple Gospel. To my surprise many of the saints told me they had seen the same thing in the Word and in the Spirit, and further, by far the greater part of all who heard it preached, accepted it.

For some time there was no great amount of persecution or opposition, but soon reports were circulated, to the effect that I was not straight in doctrine. Especially did those who for some reason were my enemies condemn and oppose me in this matter. The more I was opposed the more the Spirit moved upon me to preach it, and to challenge the opposers to find anything in the Scriptures that established the second work theory. None of them has done this, but many have brought the experience of themselves or someone else or the teaching of some man on the subject, but this does not satisfy me. I want the Word of God.

Now I find that many of the brethren see the Scripture on the finished work of Calvary just as I do, but are not preaching it. As I preach the simple truth of the Word of God: to receive Jesus, and then receive the Holy Ghost, and then live the sanctified life in the power of the Holy Ghost, God wonderfully confirms His Word with the signs following. Sinners are saved. Believers are baptized in the Holy Spirit; the sick are healed and the saints are established in Christ in a way that I never saw before.

Brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, are you going to wait till the battle is fought out and this precious truth established (for it will be established, as sure as there is a God in Heaven) and then come and take a stand for it, after the smoke of battle is cleared away? I never suffered so much for preaching any truth, nor did I ever receive such blessing. Can the brethren not see the importance of taking a stand upon the Word of God? Some say they see it, but do not think it is time to preach it. Is it ever too soon to proclaim the blessed Gospel as it is written? Others say they fear it will cause division, therefore they think best to not preach it. Can we afford to withhold the Word of God from the saints, for fear that only a part of them will receive it and thus cause a division? How would we feel toward anyone who knew the truth of God and withheld it from us, for fear we would not receive it? Jesus said, “Preach the Gospel,” not, keep still for fear of division. Again it shows a great lack of confidence in the saints, when we are afraid to trust them with the truth. I believe the saints are so in love with the truth, that most of them are willing to lay aside their prejudice and receive it, when they hear it. Further, I believe that the Spirit of God in the baptized saints, who are walking in the light, will witness to the truth when they hear it. The Word of God does not teach two works of grace, and we have no right to preach two. It teaches the finished work of the Cross, and it is our duty to preach it.

Brethren, pray and search the Word, and take your stand with me on the Word, and help fight this great battle. You will be shut out of some Missions, as I have been. You will be branded by some, for a time, as crooked; and the saints will be warned against you, as they have been against me; but you will have the joy of knowing that you are suffering for the truth, and that the reproach you are bearing is the reproach of the Cross of Jesus Christ.

The world has waited so long for the true Gospel, that it is an awful thing to fail to preach it, when it is revealed. Thank God for the large number who are falling in line with the Word, and today the Cross is being preached, as I never heard it in my life before. Brethren, hasten! the time is so short! Let us preach Christ in all His glorious fullness, and drop out all theories of men.

The Great Chicago Revival: How the Lord Poured Out His Spirit and Worked among His People

The Chicago meeting was announced as a convention to last two weeks. Brother VanLoon and the writer arrived from the Pacific Coast on the twenty-fourth of February, and the meetings commenced the twenty-fifth. Brethren Argue, McAlister and Bell, who were expected were detained at home, but we expected them a few days later. Brother Argue soon wrote us that his work in Winnipeg was in such a condition, owing to the fact that the Lord was sending in so many to hear and receive the truth, that it was impossible for him to get away. Brother McAlister wrote that unexpectedly they had to move to another hall, and therefore he could not come. All this was a very great disappointment at first, as we desired very much that this should be a convention. The Lord soon showed us, however, that His plan was to have a revival and not a convention. So we settled down into His will.

From the very first meeting the power of God was manifested. Several were baptized in the Spirit the first day. The first week twenty-eight were baptized in the Spirit with the speaking in tongues as evidence. Meantime both the interest and power were increasing. People were coming from all directions and after listening to the glorious Gospel of Christ would go to the prayer-room, and no sooner would they begin to pray than the power of God would fall upon them, and it was no unusual thing to see six or more lying under the power at the same time, and different times I saw two or more coming through speaking in tongues at the same time.

If ever I saw the proof that God is no respecter of persons, I saw it here. Old and young, black and white, without respect to creed or nationality, the people who went to seek God were met with His mighty power and baptized in the Spirit. I saw Italians, Persians, Scandinavians, Germans, Africans, Indians, Baptists, Methodists, Salvationists, in fact most all orders of people, go to the prayer-room to seek God, and saw them leave filled with the Spirit of God and heard them speaking in tongues. Time and again the power would be so great in the prayer-room that it would seem that wave after wave would surge over the people and one after another would fall under the mighty power of God and come up speaking in tongues. One night about midnight a mighty wave of power struck the seekers and between then and two o’clock five were baptized in the Spirit.

Many attended from out of town during the first two or three weeks of the revival. Almost every seeker that came in from out of town received. I only know of two who have failed. Many who came up and received have gone back to their home towns to proclaim this glorious truth. Several preachers and students are among the number who have received.

I have been in meetings where there was more noise and outward manifestations than there has been in this one. I have seen meetings where there would be much more shouting and other manifestations than we have seen here, and at the same time there would be very little definite results. But I never saw a meeting where the message of God took hold as it has here, and where there were such results as we have seen here. Of all revivals I ever attended or conducted, this in actual results has by far exceeded any. It has been a revival of results. A time when the mighty hand of God was seen all the time.

When the two weeks were up which the meeting was supposed to run, it was apparent to all that the meeting ought to go on. If I remember right the Lord had baptized thirty-three the second week and the interest was unabated. So we announced that the meetings would continue indefinitely. As we continued God was with us in the same power. Sinners would come in and get saved and many times get the baptism in the same meeting. One night seven sinners came in and were saved, and the Lord baptized four of them in the Spirit, and they spoke in tongues. That day God baptized fourteen people in the Holy Spirit. This was the greatest number we have seen in any one day since the Lord baptized us five years ago. We cannot remember to have heard of that many receiving in one day in any place since we have been in the movement. All glory, honor and praise be unto Him Who has raised up our Lord from the dead, and Who is pouring out His Spirit according to His promise. So full of praise was my heart, that for days and days it was almost continually ringing in my heart, “He hath done all things well.” When I would try to pray all I could do would be to praise Him with all my heart. Glory, glory be to His Holy Name!

Page after page might be written giving one instance after another where God proved His willingness to meet and bless His children. In fact I never saw such a manifest willingness on the part of God to work, as I have seen here. The sick have been healed in many cases. Backsliders have been restored; sinners saved in large numbers, and in nine weeks one hundred and seventy have been baptized in the Holy Spirit and spoken in tongues.

After the meetings had gone on for a few weeks, Bro. E. N. Bell came among us and was with us for several days enjoying the meetings and meantime delivered some real helpful messages. Many other ministering brethren have visited us in passing.

We are now preparing in the will of God to move to the South Side of the city to hold a revival. A large number of the saints have earnestly entreated us to do this. We find that the largest part of the seekers on the North Side have received. Will every reader of this paper pray earnestly that God will have His way in this city. He has made it plain to me that if He could have His way He would baptize thousands. We are very much in need of prayer, as the battle is exceeding hard. Two weeks ago we had to spare Bro. VanLoon from the work here as it seemed he was much needed in Los Angeles. To say that we miss him does not express it. His services were invaluable to us.

Let no one think this work has been done without opposition from the devil. In every conceivable way he has hindered and opposed. He has resorted to his same old tactics, misrepresentation, false reports, denying what God has done and in a word everything that he thought would hinder or keep any soul from coming and receiving what God has for him. All this we expect from the devil. He knows we have a Gospel that gets people to God, and he would not be the devil if he did not do everything in his power against it. In the end truth will triumph. The Finished Work of Calvary is the truth. Speaking in other tongues as the Spirit gives utterance is the evidence of the baptism in the Holy Spirit. God is honoring these blessed truths. It is not man that God honors or desires to honor. It is His own blessed truth.

Compromisers who do not preach and stand for the truth need not think that their misrepresentations will prevent God from confirming His word with signs following. Unceasing prayer has gone up to God for Chicago for months and He has answered. Let all saints everywhere join in praising Him for the great work He has done in this great, wicked city, Amen.
